By combining these two, you can build a RAG application that is not only powerful but also secure, compliant, and well-managed.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that might require it to perform a web search. Which of the following is the most appropriate LangChain component for this?
answers: A simple RAG chain.
A LangChain agent that is given a 'web search' tool.
A prompt that tells the LLM to 'search the web'.
A vector store that contains an index of the entire internet.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A simple RAG chain does not have the ability to perform a web search.

Correct: The agent architecture is specifically designed for this kind of task. The agent can use its reasoning capabilities to decide when it needs to perform a web search to answer a user's question.
Incorrect: An LLM cannot search the web on its own. It needs to be given a tool to do so.
Incorrect: While this is a fun idea, it is not a practical or a feasible solution.
questions.explanation: When a RAG application needs to be able to access real-time information from the web, the best way to do this is with a LangChain agent. You would provide the agent with a 'tool' that can perform a web search (e.g., by calling an API for a search engine like Google or DuckDuckGo). The agent's LLM can then be prompted to use this tool whenever it determines that the answer to the user's question is likely to be found on the web. This is a very powerful and a very flexible way to extend the capabilities of your RAG application beyond its local knowledge base.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a set of documents that are in PDF format. The PDFs contain a mix of text, tables, and images. Which of the following is the most effective way to process these documents for a RAG application?
answers: Using a simple text extraction library that only gets the plain text from the PDFs.
Using an advanced, multi-modal document parsing library (like `unstructured`) that can extract the text, the tables (as structured data), and can even be configured to handle the images.
Manually copying and pasting the text and the tables from each PDF.
Ignoring the tables and the images and just using the text.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would lose all the information from the tables and the images.
Correct: For complex, multi-modal documents like these, you need an advanced parsing library that can understand the different types of content and can extract them in a useful format.
Incorrect: This would be incredibly time-consuming and would not be a scalable solution.
Incorrect: This would result in the loss of a significant amount of potentially valuable information.
questions.explanation: Processing complex, multi-modal PDF documents is a challenging task. The best way to do it is to use an advanced document parsing library that is specifically designed for this purpose. A good parsing library will be able to not only extract the plain text from the PDF, but also to identify and to extract the tables in a structured format (like HTML or Markdown). Some advanced libraries can even be configured to work with the images in the PDF, for example by extracting them and by passing them to an image captioning model. By using a powerful parsing library, you can ensure that you are getting all the valuable information from your PDFs and are making it available to your RAG application.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to set up a dashboard to monitor the user engagement with the application. Which TWO of the following are the most important user engagement metrics to track?
answers: The number of CPUs used by the serving endpoint.
The number of active users per day or per week.
The session length, which is the average amount of time that a user spends interacting with the application in a single session.
The error rate of the serving endpoint.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a system-level metric, not a user engagement metric.
Correct: This is a fundamental measure of the application's reach and its adoption.
Correct: A long session length can be an indicator of high engagement, as it suggests that users are finding the application to be useful and are spending a lot of time with it.
Incorrect: This is an operational metric, not a user engagement metric.
questions.explanation: Understanding user engagement is key to understanding the success of your application. The two most important and most common user engagement metrics to track are the number of active users and the session length. The number of active users tells you how many people are using your application. The session length tells you how much they are using it. By tracking these two metrics over time, you can get a good quantitative understanding of how engaging your application is and can identify trends in its usage.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to ensure that it is highly available. They are deploying it to a single cloud region. Which of the following is the most important architectural principle to follow to achieve high availability within a single region?
answers: Deploying the application to a single, very large virtual machine.
Deploying the application across multiple, independent 'availability zones' within the region.
Using the fastest possible storage for the application's data.
Deploying the application to multiple, different cloud providers.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be a single point of failure.

Correct: All major cloud providers have the concept of availability zones, which are independent data centers within a single region. By deploying your application across multiple availability zones, you can ensure that it can survive the failure of an entire data center.
Incorrect: While this can improve performance, it does not directly affect the availability of the application.
Incorrect: This is a multi-cloud strategy, not a high-availability strategy within a single region.
questions.explanation: High availability is all about eliminating single points of failure. When you are deploying an application to a single cloud region, the key to high availability is to use multiple availability zones. An availability zone is an isolated data center within a region. By deploying your application's components (e.g., your model serving endpoints, your vector database replicas) across multiple availability zones, you can ensure that your application will continue to run even if one of the data centers has a complete failure. This is a fundamental and a critical architectural pattern for building highly available applications in the cloud.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions about a company's internal wiki. The wiki is a large collection of interconnected pages. Which of the following is the best way to represent the structure of the wiki in the RAG system's knowledge base?
answers: Ignoring the links between the pages and treating each page as a separate document.
Creating an embedding for each page and then creating a graph that represents the links between the pages. The RAG system could then use this graph to find related pages.
Creating a single, very long document that contains the text of all the pages in the wiki.
For each page, adding a list of the pages that it links to in the text that is embedded.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The links between the pages are a key part of the wiki's structure and contain valuable information.

Correct: This is a powerful, graph-based approach to RAG. By representing the wiki as a graph, you can use graph traversal algorithms to find pages that are not just semantically similar but are also structurally related, which can lead to better answers.
Incorrect: This would not be an effective or a scalable solution.

Correct: This is a simpler but also a very effective approach. By including the links in the text that is embedded, you are giving the embedding model and the LLM direct, in-band information about the structure of the wiki.
questions.explanation: When you are working with a knowledge base that has a clear graph structure, like a wiki, you should try to leverage that structure in your RAG application. The two best ways to do this are to build an explicit graph representation of the knowledge base or to include the link information directly in the text that you embed. Building a graph representation is a more complex but also a more powerful approach that can enable sophisticated graph-based retrieval strategies. A simpler but still very effective approach is to just include the links as text in your chunks. This gives the model direct context about the relationships between the pages, which can significantly improve the quality of its responses.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them as quickly as possible. They have a cluster of machines with powerful GPUs. Which of the following will be the main bottleneck in the embedding process?
answers: The speed of the network connection to the internet.
The speed at which the data can be read from the storage system and can be fed to the GPUs.
The speed of the embedding model itself.
The amount of memory on the driver node of the cluster.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The embedding process is typically a compute-bound task, not a network-bound one.

Correct: When you have very powerful GPUs, the bottleneck often shifts from the compute itself to the data pipeline that feeds the compute. If you can't get the data to the GPUs fast enough, they will be sitting idle.
Incorrect: While the model's speed is a factor, with powerful GPUs, the data pipeline is more likely to be the bottleneck.
Incorrect: The processing happens on the worker nodes, not the driver node.
questions.explanation: When you are running a large-scale, distributed embedding job on a cluster of powerful GPUs, the bottleneck is very often the data input pipeline. The GPUs are so fast at performing the actual embedding calculation that they can often process the data faster than you can get it to them. This means that the performance of your overall job is limited by the speed at which you can read the documents from your storage system (like S3 or ADLS) and can transfer them to the GPUs on the worker nodes. Building a highly optimized, high-throughput data pipeline is therefore a critical part of a high-performance embedding solution.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use a combination of automated evaluation and human evaluation. Which of the following is the best way to structure this?
answers: Using automated evaluation for everything, as human evaluation is too expensive and slow.

Using human evaluation to create a high-quality, 'golden dataset', and then using automated evaluation (with metrics like semantic similarity or an LLM-as-a-judge) to track the performance against this dataset on an ongoing basis.
Using automated evaluation to calculate a set of metrics, and then having humans review every single one of the automated scores.
Only using human evaluation for the most important questions.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While automated evaluation is great for scale, human evaluation is the gold standard for quality and is essential for validating the automated metrics.

Correct: This is the standard and most effective way to combine human and automated evaluation. The humans create the ground truth, and the automated systems use that ground truth to provide a continuous, scalable evaluation.
Incorrect: This would defeat the purpose of the automated evaluation, which is to provide a scalable solution.
Incorrect: While a good idea, this is not a complete strategy. You need a way to track the performance on a wider range of questions, which is where the automated evaluation comes in.
questions.explanation: The best way to evaluate a RAG application is to use a hybrid approach that combines the strengths of both human and automated evaluation. The ideal workflow is to first use a team of human experts to create a high-quality 'golden dataset' of question-answer pairs. This dataset represents the ground truth for your application. You can then use this golden dataset to power an automated evaluation pipeline. This pipeline can run on a regular basis and can use automated metrics to track the application's performance against the ground truth. This gives you the best of both worlds: the quality and the nuance of human judgment, and the speed and the scalability of automated evaluation.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to ensure that it is secure. Which of the following is the most important security principle to follow?
answers: The principle of 'defense in depth', which means having multiple, independent layers of security controls.
The principle of 'security through obscurity', which means keeping the details of your system secret.
The principle of 'move fast and break things'.
The principle of 'trust the user'.
feedbacks: Correct: Defense in depth is a fundamental security principle. It means that you should not rely on a single security control, but should instead have multiple layers of defense. For a RAG application, this might include input validation, access control on the data, content moderation, and network security.
Incorrect: This is a widely discredited security principle. A truly secure system should be secure even if the attacker knows everything about how it works.
Incorrect: This is a product development philosophy, not a security principle. In fact, it's often the opposite of what you want for a secure system.
Incorrect: For security, you should follow the principle of 'zero trust', which means that you should not automatically trust any user or any component of the system.
questions.explanation: Defense in depth is one of the most important and most widely accepted principles of information security. The idea is that no single security control is perfect, so you should always have multiple layers of defense. If one layer fails, you have other layers to back it up. For a RAG application, this means thinking about security at every level of the stack: at the network level, at the data level, at the application level, and at the model level. By implementing a multi-layered security strategy, you can build a much more robust and a much more resilient application.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to be able to have a long, coherent conversation with a user. Which of the following is the best type of memory to use for this?
answers: A `ConversationBufferMemory`, which stores the entire conversation history.
A `ConversationBufferWindowMemory`, which only stores the last K turns of the conversation.
A `ConversationSummaryMemory`, which uses an LLM to create a summary of the conversation as it progresses.
No memory at all.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this would work for short conversations, it would quickly exceed the LLM's context window for a long conversation.
Correct: This is a good choice for keeping the memory from growing too large. It ensures that the LLM always has the most recent context.

Correct: This is a very powerful technique for long conversations. Instead of storing the entire history, you store a running summary. This allows the agent to 'remember' the key points of a very long conversation without exceeding the context window.
Incorrect: The application would not be able to have a coherent conversation without memory.
questions.explanation: For long conversations, you need a memory strategy that can gracefully handle a large number of turns without exceeding the LLM's context window. The two best approaches for this are to use a windowed buffer memory or a summary memory. A windowed buffer memory is a simple and an effective approach that just keeps the last K turns of the conversation. A summary memory is a more advanced and a more powerful technique. It uses an LLM to create a running summary of the conversation. This allows the agent to have a very long and a very coherent conversation, as the summary can capture the key information from the entire history in a very compact form.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is simple to implement and is computationally efficient. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Semantic chunking.
Fixed-size chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Using a large language model to decide on the optimal chunk boundaries.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Semantic chunking is computationally expensive.
Correct: This is the simplest and the most computationally efficient chunking strategy.
Correct: While slightly more complex than fixed-size chunking, a recursive splitter is still very computationally efficient and is easy to implement.
Incorrect: This would be a very powerful but also a very computationally expensive approach.
questions.explanation: When simplicity and computational efficiency are the top priorities for a chunking strategy, the two best choices are fixed-size chunking and recursive character text splitting. Fixed-size chunking is the absolute simplest and fastest method. A recursive character text splitter is also very fast and is only slightly more complex to implement, but it has the advantage of being more semantically aware than a simple fixed-size chunker. For many applications, one of these two simple and efficient strategies is all that is needed.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use A/B testing to compare two different LLMs. Which of the following is the most important metric to use for this A/B test?
answers: The latency of the responses from the two models.
The user satisfaction with the responses from the two models, as measured by a feedback mechanism.
The cost of the two models.
The number of tokens generated by the two models.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While latency is an important operational metric, the primary goal of this A/B test is to compare the quality of the two models.
Correct: The ultimate measure of a model's quality is how helpful it is to the users. A user satisfaction metric is the best way to measure this.
Incorrect: While cost is an important business consideration, it is not the primary metric for evaluating the quality of the models in an A/B test.
Incorrect: This is an attribute of the responses, not a measure of their quality.
questions.explanation: When you are A/B testing two different LLMs, the most important thing you want to know is which one provides a better experience for your users. The best way to measure this is with a user satisfaction metric. By randomly showing users the responses from one of the two models and then collecting their feedback (e.g., with a 'thumbs up' / 'thumbs down' rating), you can get a direct, quantitative measure of which model the users prefer. This is the most important and the most relevant metric for making a decision between the two models.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and has a strict requirement that all of its infrastructure must be deployed as code, to ensure that the environments are repeatable and are auditable. Which TWO of the following technologies are most important for achieving this?
answers: A set of manual deployment instructions in a Word document.
An infrastructure-as-code (IaC) tool, such as Terraform or Bicep, to define and to manage the cloud resources (like the Databricks workspace and the networking).
A CI/CD pipeline that uses the IaC tool to automatically deploy and to update the infrastructure.
A team of operations engineers who can manually create the infrastructure.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the opposite of 'infrastructure as code'.
Correct: An IaC tool is the foundation of an infrastructure-as-code strategy. It allows you to define all your infrastructure in a set of version-controlled, declarative configuration files.

Correct: The CI/CD pipeline is what brings the 'code' in 'infrastructure as code' to life. It automates the process of applying the IaC configuration, which makes the deployments fast, reliable, and repeatable.
Incorrect: The goal of infrastructure as code is to automate the work of the operations team, not to rely on them for manual tasks.
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code (IaC) is a key practice of modern DevOps and MLOps. It's the idea that all your infrastructure should be defined and be managed in a set of version-controlled code files. The two key technologies for this are an IaC tool and a CI/CD pipeline. The IaC tool (like Terraform) is what you use to write the declarative configuration for your infrastructure. The CI/CD pipeline is what you use to automatically apply that configuration. By combining these two, you can create a fully automated, a fully auditable, and a fully repeatable process for managing your RAG application's infrastructure.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and has found that the LLM is sometimes making up answers that are not supported by the retrieved documents. This problem is known as:
answers: Hallucination.
Contextual irrelevance.
Prompt injection.
Overfitting.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the standard industry term for when an LLM generates text that is factually incorrect or is not grounded in the provided context.
Incorrect: Contextual irrelevance is when the retrieved documents are not relevant to the query. This is a problem with the retriever, not with the generator.
Incorrect: Prompt injection is a security vulnerability where a user tries to manipulate the LLM's behavior.
Incorrect: Overfitting is a concept from traditional machine learning and is not the correct term for this phenomenon in generative AI.
questions.explanation: The tendency of large language models to sometimes generate text that is plausible-sounding but is factually incorrect is known as 'hallucination'. In the context of a RAG application, a hallucination occurs when the LLM generates an answer that is not supported by the information in the retrieved documents. Minimizing hallucinations and maximizing the 'faithfulness' of the LLM to the provided context is one of the most important goals in building a high-quality and a trustworthy RAG application.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is robust and that will work well for a wide variety of document types. They are not as concerned about the computational cost. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Semantic chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Sentence-level chunking.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a robust strategy.

Correct: If computational cost is not a concern, semantic chunking is often the highest quality and the most robust chunking strategy. It uses the meaning of the text to find the optimal chunk boundaries, which works well on any type of document.
Correct: A well-configured recursive splitter is also a very robust and a very good general-purpose choice. It is often a good compromise between quality and computational cost.
Incorrect: This is not as robust as the other two options for a heterogeneous dataset.
questions.explanation: When quality and robustness are the top priorities and computational cost is less of a concern, the two best chunking strategies are semantic chunking and recursive character text splitting. Semantic chunking is the state-of-the-art in terms of quality, as it uses an AI model to find the true semantic boundaries in the text. A recursive character text splitter is a very powerful heuristic-based approach that can also be very effective and is often a good default choice for any RAG application.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to monitor it for any unexpected or anomalous behavior. Which of the following is the most effective way to do this on Databricks?
answers: Manually inspecting the application's logs every day.
Using Databricks Lakehouse Monitoring to automatically track the statistical properties of the application's inputs and outputs and to alert on any significant drift or any outliers.
Assuming that the application will always behave as expected.
Writing a set of simple rules to check for specific known failure modes.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a scalable or a reliable way to detect anomalies.

Correct: Lakehouse Monitoring is specifically designed for this purpose. It can automatically learn the expected distribution of your data and can then alert you if it detects any significant deviations from that distribution.
Incorrect: All production systems can have unexpected behavior, and it's important to have a system in place to monitor for it.

Incorrect: While this can be a part of a monitoring strategy, it will not be able to detect unknown or unexpected anomalies. A statistical approach like the one used by Lakehouse Monitoring is needed for that.
questions.explanation: Detecting unexpected anomalies in a production AI system is a critical part of a robust monitoring strategy. On Databricks, the best tool for this is Lakehouse Monitoring. It can be configured to automatically monitor the data that is flowing through your RAG application (e.g., the user queries, the retrieved documents, the generated answers). It will learn the normal statistical properties of this data and will then automatically alert you if it detects any significant drift or any outliers. This provides a powerful, automated safety net that can help you to quickly identify and to respond to any unexpected behavior in your application.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that the access to the underlying data is securely managed. They have a policy that all access to data must be granted through groups, not to individual users. Which TWO of the following Unity Catalog features are essential for implementing this policy?
answers: The ability to create tables.
The ability to create groups of users.
The ability to grant permissions (e.g., `SELECT`) on a data asset (like a table) to a group.
The ability to run SQL queries.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While you need tables to store the data, this is not the feature that is used to manage access.
Correct: The first step is to create groups that correspond to the different roles or teams that will need access to the data.
Correct: The second step is to grant the necessary permissions on the data to the groups that you have created. This is the core of the access control model.
Incorrect: This is how you access the data, not how you manage the access to it.
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog provides a robust and a flexible access control model that is based on the standard SQL concepts of users, groups, and grants. To implement a policy where all access is managed through groups, you would use two key features. First, you would use the `CREATE GROUP` command to create the groups that represent the different personas in your organization. Second, you would use the `GRANT` command to give the necessary permissions on the data assets to those groups. This is a standard and a very scalable best practice for managing access control in any data platform.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain agent and wants to provide it with a set of tools. What is the most important information that needs to be provided for each tool?
answers: The name of the tool.
A clear and a concise description of what the tool does.
The full source code of the tool.
The name of the developer who created the tool.
feedbacks: Correct: The name of the tool is how the LLM will refer to it when it decides to use it.
Correct: The description is the most important piece of information. The LLM will use this description to understand what the tool is for and when it should be used.
Incorrect: The LLM does not need to see the source code of the tool. It only needs to know what the tool does.
Incorrect: This is irrelevant information for the LLM.
questions.explanation: When you are giving a set of tools to a LangChain agent, the two most important pieces of information that you need to provide for each tool are its name and its description. The name is the unique identifier for the tool. The description is what the LLM will use to understand the tool's purpose. A well-written, clear, and a concise description is critical for the agent to be able to make an intelligent decision about which tool to use for a given task.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is both effective and easy to debug. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Semantic chunking.
Fixed-size chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Using an LLM to determine the chunk boundaries.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Semantic chunking can be difficult to debug, as the chunk boundaries are determined by a black-box embedding model.
Correct: Fixed-size chunking is very easy to debug, as the logic is extremely simple and deterministic.
Correct: A recursive splitter is also relatively easy to debug. The logic is deterministic, and you can easily trace how a document was split by looking at the separators.
Incorrect: This would be the most difficult to debug, as the behavior of the LLM would be non-deterministic and hard to interpret.
questions.explanation: When debuggability is a key concern for a chunking strategy, you want to choose a method that is simple and deterministic. The two best choices for this are fixed-size chunking and recursive character text splitting. With a fixed-size chunker, you can always know exactly why a chunk was created. With a recursive splitter, the logic is also very transparent and easy to trace. This is in contrast to a more complex, AI-powered technique like semantic chunking, where it can be very difficult to understand why the model decided to create a chunk boundary at a particular point in the text.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to evaluate it. They do not have a golden dataset. Which TWO of the following are the most effective evaluation techniques in this scenario?
answers: Calculating the semantic similarity between the generated answer and a pre-defined correct answer.
Using an LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate the quality of the responses on metrics like faithfulness and answer relevancy.
Collecting and analyzing user feedback.
Calculating the BLEU score of the generated answers.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This requires a golden dataset.
Correct: LLM-as-a-judge is a powerful technique that does not require a golden dataset. It can evaluate the quality of a response based only on the user's query and the retrieved context.
Correct: User feedback is another excellent evaluation technique that does not require a golden dataset. It provides a direct signal of the users' perceived quality of the application.
Incorrect: BLEU score requires a set of reference (i.e., golden) answers.
questions.explanation: When you don't have a golden dataset, you need to use 'unsupervised' or 'reference-free' evaluation techniques. The two most powerful and most common such techniques are LLM-as-a-judge and user feedback analysis. The LLM-as-a-judge approach allows you to get a scalable, automated measure of the quality of your application's responses without needing any pre-labeled data. User feedback analysis allows you to get a direct signal from your users about what they think of the application. The combination of these two techniques can provide a surprisingly comprehensive picture of your application's performance, even without a golden dataset.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by its entire organization. They want to ensure that the application is developed and is deployed in a way that is consistent with their MLOps best practices. Which TWO of the following are the most important aspects of this?
answers: Ensuring that the entire application is developed by a single 'hero' developer.
Ensuring that all the code for the application is stored and is versioned in a centralized Git repository.
Ensuring that the process of testing and of deploying the application is fully automated with a CI/CD pipeline.
Ensuring that the application is deployed manually to ensure maximum control.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the opposite of a good MLOps practice, which emphasizes collaboration and shared ownership.
Correct: Version control is the foundation of all modern MLOps practices.
Correct: Automation through CI/CD is a cornerstone of MLOps.
Incorrect: Manual deployments are error-prone and are not consistent with MLOps best practices.
questions.explanation: MLOps is all about bringing the principles of DevOps to the world of machine learning. The two most fundamental of these principles are to use version control for everything and to automate everything. By using a centralized Git repository for all the code and the other assets of your RAG application, you create a single source of truth and you enable collaboration and reproducibility. By using a CI/CD pipeline to automate the testing and the deployment of your application, you make the process faster, more reliable, and more consistent. These two practices are the foundation of a mature MLOps for RAG workflow.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that are very sensitive to the exact wording of the source documents, such as legal or medical questions. Which of the following RAG architectures would be most appropriate?
answers: A summarization-based RAG architecture.
An extractive RAG architecture, where the LLM is specifically instructed to extract the answer as a direct quote from the source document.
An agent-based architecture that can consult multiple external experts.
A RAG architecture that also provides a link to the exact source document and highlights the passage from which the answer was extracted.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Summarization can lose important details and nuances from the source text, which would be dangerous for a legal or a medical application.

Correct: For use cases where precision and fidelity to the source text are critical, an extractive approach is the best. By forcing the LLM to extract the answer as a verbatim quote, you can be much more confident that it is not misinterpreting or misrepresenting the information.
Incorrect: While an interesting idea, this is not a standard or a practical architecture for this kind of task.

Correct: This is a critical feature for any high-stakes RAG application. By providing a clear and a direct link back to the source, you allow the user to easily verify the information for themselves, which is essential for building trust.
questions.explanation: For a high-stakes RAG application that deals with sensitive and precise information, the two most important architectural principles are to be extractive and to be transparent. An extractive architecture, where the LLM is forced to find the answer as a direct quote from the source, minimizes the risk of the LLM hallucinating or misinterpreting the information. A transparent architecture, where the application provides a clear link back to the source document and highlights the relevant passage, allows the user to easily verify the answer for themselves. The combination of these two principles is the key to building a trustworthy and a reliable RAG application for any critical use case.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that are stored in a Delta table. They want to create embeddings for a specific text column in the table. Which of the following is the most efficient way to do this in a Spark job?
answers: Collecting the entire column to the driver node as a list of strings and then processing it there.
Using a Pandas UDF that takes the text column as a Pandas Series, calls an embedding model on the series, and returns a new Pandas Series with the embeddings.
Using a row-at-a-time UDF.
Writing the column to a text file and then reading it back in a different job.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be scalable and would likely cause the driver to run out of memory.

Correct: This is the standard and most performant way to apply a function like an embedding model to a column of a Spark DataFrame. It leverages both the distributed nature of Spark and the efficiency of vectorized libraries like Pandas.
Incorrect: A row-at-a-time UDF would be very slow due to the high overhead of serialization and function invocation for each row.
Incorrect: This would be a very inefficient and an unnecessary intermediate step.
questions.explanation: When you need to apply a complex function to a column of a Spark DataFrame, a Pandas UDF is almost always the best choice for performance. It works by taking a batch of rows for a given column, converting it to a Pandas Series, and then applying your Python function to that entire series at once. This is much more efficient than a row-at-a-time UDF, as it significantly reduces the overhead of data serialization and allows you to use highly optimized libraries that work on vectorized data. For a task like embedding generation, a Pandas UDF is the key to achieving high performance and scalability.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that it has a robust governance model. Which of the following is the most important principle of a good AI governance model?
answers: To move as fast as possible and to worry about governance later.
To have a centralized, unified system for managing all the data and the AI assets of the organization, with clear policies for access control, lineage, and auditing.
To give every developer full admin access to all the systems to empower them.
To treat governance as a purely technical problem that can be solved with a single tool.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a recipe for disaster. Governance needs to be a key consideration from the very beginning of the project.
Correct: This is the essence of a good governance model. A centralized, unified approach ensures that the governance is consistent, is comprehensive, and is easy to manage.
Incorrect: This would be a major security risk and would be the opposite of a good governance model.
Incorrect: Governance is a socio-technical problem that involves people, processes, and tools. A good governance model needs to address all three of these aspects.
questions.explanation: A good AI governance model is not just about tools; it's about a holistic approach that combines people, processes, and technology. However, the cornerstone of a modern, effective governance model is a centralized, unified system for managing all the data and the AI assets of the organization. On Databricks, this is the role of Unity Catalog. By providing a single pane of glass for all your data and AI, Unity Catalog allows you to implement consistent policies for access control, to automatically track data lineage, and to maintain a comprehensive audit trail. This provides the technical foundation for a robust and a trustworthy governance framework.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain application and wants to create a chain that takes a user's question, passes it to two different LLMs in parallel, and then combines their answers. Which of the following is the best way to do this in LCEL?
answers: `answer1 = llm1.predict(question); answer2 = llm2.predict(question)`
`{'answer1': llm1, 'answer2': llm2} | combine_answers_func`
`(llm1, llm2) | combine_answers_func`
`llm1 | llm2 | combine_answers_func`
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is just standard Python code and does not create a composable LCEL chain.

Correct: This is the perfect use case for `RunnableParallel` (which can be expressed as a dictionary). It will run both LLMs in parallel and will pass a dictionary containing both of their answers to the next step in the chain.
Incorrect: This is not the correct syntax for parallel execution in LCEL. You need to use a dictionary or a `RunnableParallel` object.
Incorrect: This would create a sequential chain, where the output of the first LLM is passed as the input to the second.
questions.explanation: LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) makes it very easy to perform operations in parallel. The key to this is the `RunnableParallel` class, which can be conveniently expressed as a simple dictionary. By creating a dictionary where each value is a `Runnable` object (like an LLM), you can instruct LCEL to run all of those `Runnable` objects in parallel. The output of this parallel step will be a dictionary where the keys are the same as the keys in your input dictionary, and the values are the outputs of the corresponding `Runnable` objects. This is a very powerful and a very common pattern for a wide range of tasks, such as comparing the outputs of two different models.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is aware of the document's structure. The documents are a mix of prose and source code. Which of the following is the best chunking strategy?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Using a text splitter that can be configured with a specific programming language, which allows it to intelligently split the code based on its syntax (e.g., by functions or classes).
Using a recursive character text splitter with a set of separators that are appropriate for both prose and code.
Treating the entire document as a single chunk.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a structure-aware strategy and would likely break up the code in a way that makes it invalid.

Correct: For documents that contain source code, the best approach is to use a language-aware text splitter. This will ensure that the code is chunked in a way that preserves its syntactic and its semantic integrity.

Correct: This is another good and a more general-purpose approach. You can create a hierarchy of separators that can handle the structure of both the natural language parts and the code parts of the document.
Incorrect: This would not be a scalable or an effective approach.
questions.explanation: When you are working with documents that contain source code, a simple chunking strategy is not enough. You need a strategy that is 'language-aware' and that can respect the structure of the code. The two best ways to do this are to use a specialized, language-aware text splitter or to use a well-configured recursive character text splitter. A language-aware splitter can parse the code and can make intelligent decisions about where to split it (e.g., at the end of a function). A recursive splitter can be configured with a set of separators that are designed to work well for both the code and the surrounding text. Both of these approaches will produce much higher-quality chunks than a simple, structure-agnostic method.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to monitor its performance. They are particularly interested in the user experience. Which TWO of the following are the most important user-centric metrics to track?
answers: The CPU utilization of the serving endpoint.
The user satisfaction score, as measured by a feedback mechanism.
The task success rate, which is the percentage of users who are able to successfully complete their intended task with the application.
The number of embeddings in the vector database.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a system-level metric, not a user-centric one.
Correct: This is a direct measure of how helpful the users are finding the application.
Correct: This is another excellent, user-centric metric. It measures whether the application is actually helping users to achieve their goals.
Incorrect: This is a system-level metric and is not directly related to the user experience.
questions.explanation: When you are monitoring the performance of a RAG application, it's important to go beyond system-level metrics and to track the metrics that reflect the actual user experience. The two most important user-centric metrics are user satisfaction and task success rate. User satisfaction tells you what the users think about the application. The task success rate tells you if the application is actually working for them. By tracking these two metrics, you can get a clear and an actionable picture of the quality of your application from the user's point of view.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that all the infrastructure for the application can be managed as code. Which of the following is the primary benefit of this 'infrastructure as code' approach?
answers: It makes the infrastructure cheaper to run.
It makes the infrastructure deployments repeatable, consistent, and auditable.
It eliminates the need for an operations team.
It makes the application run faster.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While it can lead to cost savings through efficiency, the primary benefit is not about the direct cost of the infrastructure.

Correct: The primary benefit of IaC is that it brings the discipline of software engineering to the management of infrastructure. By defining your infrastructure in code, you make it easy to create consistent, repeatable, and version-controlled environments.
Incorrect: It changes the role of the operations team from one of manual configuration to one of managing the IaC code and the automation pipelines.
Incorrect: The performance of the application is not directly affected by whether the infrastructure is managed as code.
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code (IaC) is a fundamental practice of modern DevOps and MLOps. Its primary benefit is that it makes the process of provisioning and of managing your infrastructure repeatable, consistent, and auditable. By defining your entire environment in a set of version-controlled code files, you can eliminate the manual, error-prone processes of the past. This allows you to spin up a new environment with the push of a button, to ensure that your development and your production environments are identical, and to have a complete audit trail of every change that has ever been made to your infrastructure.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and has found that for some ambiguous queries, the LLM is not sure how to respond. The developer wants the application to ask the user for clarification in these cases. Which of the following is the best way to implement this?
answers: Fine-tuning the LLM to be better at handling ambiguous queries.
Using a LangChain agent that has a 'human-in-the-loop' tool.
Always asking the user for clarification, even for simple queries.
Trying to guess what the user meant and providing an answer based on that guess.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this might help, it doesn't solve the fundamental problem of what to do when the model is still unsure. An agent-based approach is better for this.

Correct: LangChain and other frameworks provide tools for 'human-in-the-loop' workflows. The agent can be designed to recognize when it is not confident in its answer, and it can then use the human-in-the-loop tool to ask the user for clarification.
Incorrect: This would lead to a very poor user experience.
Incorrect: This is likely to lead to incorrect answers and a frustrated user. It's better to ask for clarification when you are not sure.
questions.explanation: Handling ambiguity is a key challenge in building conversational AI applications. The best way to do it is to give the application the ability to ask for help when it needs it. A 'human-in-the-loop' architecture is designed for this exact purpose. In a LangChain agent, you can create a tool that allows the agent to pause its execution and to ask the user a clarifying question. The agent can be prompted to use this tool whenever its confidence in its own answer is low. This creates a much more robust and a much more user-friendly experience than just trying to guess what the user meant.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use an LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate its responses. Which TWO of the following are the most important characteristics of a good 'judge' LLM?
answers: It should be very small and fast.
It should have strong reasoning and instruction-following capabilities.
It should be a model that has been specifically fine-tuned for the domain of the RAG application.
It should be from the same family of models as the LLM that is being evaluated.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A larger, more capable LLM is generally a better and a more reliable judge.

Correct: The judge LLM needs to be able to understand a complex rubric and to consistently apply it to the responses it is evaluating. This requires strong reasoning and instruction-following abilities.
Incorrect: It is often better to use a general-purpose, state-of-the-art model as the judge, as it is less likely to be biased towards the specific content of the application's domain.
Incorrect: It is often better to use a model from a different provider or a different family as the judge, to reduce the risk of a shared bias.
questions.explanation: When you are choosing an LLM to act as a judge for your RAG application, you want to choose a model that is as capable and as objective as possible. This means that you should generally choose a large, state-of-the-art model that is known for its strong reasoning and its instruction-following capabilities. Models like GPT-4 are often used for this purpose. It is also often a good idea to choose a judge model that is from a different family or a different provider than the model you are evaluating. This can help to reduce the risk that the judge will have the same inherent biases as the model it is judging, which can lead to a more objective and a more reliable evaluation.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and has a requirement that all data and all models must be hosted in their own private cloud environment. Which TWO of the following are the most significant challenges of this approach, compared to using managed services?
answers: It provides a higher level of security.
It requires a significant amount of engineering effort and expertise to deploy, to manage, and to maintain the infrastructure for the LLM and the vector database.
It can be more difficult to get access to the latest, state-of-the-art models, as these are often only available as proprietary, managed APIs.
It is always more expensive.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While it provides more control, it does not necessarily provide a higher level of security. A well-configured managed service can be very secure.
Correct: This is the biggest challenge of a self-hosted approach. You are taking on the full operational burden of managing a complex, distributed system.
Correct: The leading AI research labs often keep their best models proprietary. With a self-hosted approach, you are limited to the best available open-source models.
Incorrect: At very large scale, a self-hosted approach can sometimes be more cost-effective than using a pay-per-use API.
questions.explanation: While a self-hosted approach to RAG provides the maximum level of control, it also comes with a number of significant challenges. The two biggest of these are the operational complexity and the access to models. Deploying, managing, and scaling a large language model and a vector database is a major engineering undertaking that requires a specialized skillset. In addition, by limiting yourself to open-source models, you may not be able to get access to the same level of performance and capability as the state-of-the-art proprietary models that are available through a managed API. These trade-offs need to be carefully considered when choosing an architecture for a RAG application.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and has found that for some questions, the LLM's response is too short and is not very helpful. Which of the following is the most effective prompt engineering technique to encourage the LLM to provide a more detailed and a more comprehensive answer?
answers: Using a very concise prompt.
Using a 'chain-of-thought' prompt, where you explicitly ask the LLM to 'think step-by-step' before providing the final answer.
Assigning an 'expert' persona to the LLM in the prompt, for example, 'You are a world-renowned expert in this topic. Provide a detailed and a comprehensive explanation.'
Using a smaller and a less capable LLM.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A concise prompt is more likely to lead to a concise answer.
Correct: Chain-of-thought prompting is a powerful technique for getting more detailed and more well-reasoned responses from an LLM.
Correct: Giving the LLM an expert persona can be a very effective way to encourage it to generate a more detailed and a more confident response.
Incorrect: A smaller LLM is less likely to be able to provide a detailed and a comprehensive answer.
questions.explanation: When you want an LLM to provide a more detailed and a more comprehensive response, you need to give it a prompt that encourages that kind of behavior. The two most effective techniques for this are chain-of-thought prompting and persona assignment. Chain-of-thought prompting explicitly asks the model to lay out its reasoning process, which often leads to a more thorough and a more well-structured answer. Assigning an expert persona to the model can also be very effective. It seems to encourage the model to access the more detailed and the more nuanced information from its training data, which results in a higher quality and a more comprehensive response.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create a vector index that is both fast to query and that can be updated incrementally. Which of the following is the best solution on Databricks?
answers: A DIRECT index in Databricks Vector Search.
A DELTA_SYNC index in Databricks Vector Search.
A FAISS index that is re-built from scratch every day.
A Chroma DB index that is updated by a custom streaming application.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A DIRECT index is fast, but it cannot be updated incrementally.
Correct: A DELTA_SYNC index is the perfect solution for this. It is designed to be updated incrementally from a source Delta table, and it is highly optimized for fast query performance.
Incorrect: This would not be an incremental solution.
Incorrect: While a possible solution, a DELTA_SYNC index in Databricks Vector Search is a much more integrated, a much more managed, and a much more robust solution on the Databricks platform.
questions.explanation: For a RAG application that needs both fast queries and incremental updates, the `DELTA_SYNC` index in Databricks Vector Search is the ideal solution. It provides the best of both worlds. It is designed to automatically and efficiently stay in sync with a source Delta table, which makes it easy to keep the index up-to-date. At the same time, it is built on a highly optimized, high-performance architecture that is designed to provide low-latency query responses. This makes it the perfect choice for most production RAG applications on Databricks.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use an A/B test to compare the performance of two different prompts. Which of the following is the most important part of the methodology for this A/B test?
answers: Showing both prompts to each user and asking them which one they prefer.
Randomly assigning each user to either the 'A' group (who see the old prompt) or the 'B' group (who see the new prompt).
Using a very small number of users for the test.
Choosing the prompt that the development team likes the best.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a preference test, not a standard A/B test. In an A/B test, each user only sees one version.
Correct: Random assignment is the cornerstone of A/B testing. It is what allows you to make a causal inference about the effect of the new prompt.
Incorrect: To get a statistically significant result, you need to have a sufficiently large number of users in each group.
Incorrect: The goal of the A/B test is to get objective, data-driven evidence of which prompt is better, not to go with the subjective opinion of the development team.
questions.explanation: The single most important part of the methodology for any A/B test is the random assignment of users to the different groups. By randomly assigning users to either the control group (A) or the treatment group (B), you can ensure that, on average, the two groups are identical in every way except for the one thing you are testing (in this case, the prompt). This is what allows you to be confident that any difference you observe in the outcome metric is actually caused by the change you made, and is not just due to some other pre-existing difference between the two groups of users.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that they have a clear and an auditable record of all the changes that are made to the application's code and its AI models. Which TWO of the following are the most important tools for this?
answers: A version control system, such as Git, for managing the application's code.
A model registry, such as the MLflow Model Registry, for versioning the AI models.
A shared network drive where developers can store their code.
A project management tool where developers can log the changes they have made.
feedbacks: Correct: A version control system is the essential tool for tracking the history of the code. It provides a complete and an auditable record of every change that has been made.

Correct: A model registry is the equivalent of a version control system for your AI models. It allows you to version, to document, and to manage your models, which provides a clear audit trail of their history.
Incorrect: This would not provide any version control or audit capabilities.
Incorrect: While useful for tracking tasks, a project management tool is not a substitute for a proper version control system.
questions.explanation: To have a clear and an auditable record of all the changes to a RAG application, you need to use a version control system for the code and a model registry for the AI models. A version control system like Git is the standard tool for managing the history of any software project. A model registry like the one in MLflow is the standard tool for managing the history of any AI model. By using both of these, you can create a comprehensive and a fully auditable record of the entire history of your RAG application, which is a key requirement for good governance and for reproducibility.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain agent and wants to give it access to a set of custom Python functions. Which of the following is the best way to turn these functions into 'tools' that the agent can use?
answers: Simply passing the Python function objects to the agent.
Using the `@tool` decorator from LangChain to automatically convert the Python functions into `Tool` objects.
Manually creating a `Tool` object for each function, providing a name, the function itself, and a description.
Asking the LLM to write the code for the tools.
feedbacks: Incorrect: You need to wrap the functions in a `Tool` object to provide the necessary name and description.

Correct: The `@tool` decorator is a very convenient and a very idiomatic way to create tools from your Python functions. It automatically uses the function's name and its docstring to create the name and the description for the tool.

Correct: This is the more explicit way to create a tool. It gives you more control over the name and the description, which can be useful if you want them to be different from the function's name and its docstring.
Incorrect: The LLM can't write the tools for you. You need to provide the tools to the agent.
questions.explanation: LangChain makes it very easy to turn any Python function into a tool that an agent can use. The two best ways to do this are to use the `@tool` decorator or to manually create a `Tool` object. The `@tool` decorator is the simplest and the most convenient approach. You just add it to your function definition, and LangChain will automatically create a tool from it. Manually creating a `Tool` object is a more explicit approach that gives you more control over how the tool is defined. Both are excellent and a very common pattern for building custom tools for a LangChain agent.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that will create the most semantically coherent chunks, without regard to the computational cost. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Semantic chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Sentence-level chunking.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the least semantically coherent strategy.
Correct: Semantic chunking is the state-of-the-art for creating semantically coherent chunks. It uses an embedding model to find the natural topic boundaries in the text.
Incorrect: While a good heuristic, it is not as semantically coherent as true semantic chunking.
Incorrect: While better than fixed-size, it is still not as semantically coherent as semantic chunking.
questions.explanation: When the absolute highest quality and the most semantically coherent chunks are the top priority, the best chunking strategy is semantic chunking. Unlike all other common strategies, which are based on the syntactic structure of the text, semantic chunking is based on the meaning of the text. It uses a sophisticated AI model to analyze the document and to find the natural breaking points where the topic or the context changes. This results in chunks that are much more likely to represent a single, coherent idea, which can lead to a significant improvement in the performance of a RAG system.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to set up a system for continuous evaluation. Which of the following is the most important component of this system?
answers: A team of dedicated human evaluators.
A high-quality, representative, and a stable 'golden dataset' of test cases.
A very fast and a very powerful cluster for running the evaluations.
A user interface that allows the developers to easily see the results of the evaluations.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While human evaluation is important for creating the initial test set, it is not a scalable solution for continuous evaluation.
Correct: The golden dataset is the foundation of a continuous evaluation system. It provides the stable ground truth that all future versions of the application can be compared against.
Incorrect: While performance is nice to have, the quality and the stability of the test set are much more important.
Incorrect: While a good UI is important for usability, the golden dataset itself is the most critical component of the system.
questions.explanation: The most important component of any continuous evaluation system is the 'golden dataset'. This is a carefully curated set of test cases that are representative of the key capabilities of your application. This dataset provides the stable, unchanging ground truth that you can use to measure the performance of your application over time. Without a high-quality golden dataset, it is impossible to know if a change in your evaluation metrics is due to a real change in your application's performance or is just due to a change in the test cases themselves.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions about a company's products. The product information is stored in a structured format in a Delta table. Which of the following is the most effective architecture for this?
answers: A RAG chain that retrieves the entire Delta table and passes it to the LLM.
A 'Text-to-SQL' agent that can convert the user's natural language question into a SQL query, can run the query against the Delta table, and can then use the results to generate an answer.
An extractive RAG chain that works on a text-based representation of the Delta table.
A summarization-based RAG chain.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be scalable and would likely exceed the LLM's context window.
Correct: This is the state-of-the-art approach for question-answering on structured data. It combines the natural language understanding of the LLM with the power and the precision of a SQL database.
Incorrect: While possible, this would not be as effective or as precise as a Text-to-SQL approach.
Incorrect: Summarization is not the right approach for querying a structured database.
questions.explanation: When the knowledge for a RAG application is stored in a structured database like a Delta table, a Text-to-SQL architecture is the most powerful and the most effective solution. This architecture uses an LLM-powered agent to act as a 'translator' between the user's natural language and the formal language of SQL. The agent can understand the user's question, can generate the correct SQL query to retrieve the answer from the database, and can then use the results of that query to generate a natural language response. This is a much more powerful and a much more flexible approach than trying to treat the structured data as unstructured text.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them. They have a limited budget and a large number of documents. Which of the following is the most cost-effective way to create the embeddings on Databricks?
answers: Using the largest, most powerful GPU cluster available.
Using a small, efficient open-source embedding model and hosting it on a CPU-based cluster.
Using a managed foundation model API from Databricks, and taking advantage of any available optimizations and pricing tiers.
Using a third-party embedding API that charges a high price per document.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be the most expensive option.
Correct: For cost-sensitive, large-scale embedding tasks, a small, efficient open-source model running on a CPU cluster can be a very cost-effective solution.
Correct: The managed embedding models from Databricks are often highly optimized for cost and performance, and they can be a very good option for teams that want a managed solution.
Incorrect: This would not be a cost-effective solution.
questions.explanation: When cost is the primary driver for an embedding project, you need to find the right balance between the cost of the compute and the cost of the model. On Databricks, there are two great, cost-effective options. The first is to use a small, efficient open-source model and to run it on a CPU-based cluster. This 'do-it-yourself' approach can be very cheap at scale. The second option is to use one of the managed embedding models from Databricks. These models are often highly optimized for the platform and are priced very competitively, and they have the added benefit of being a fully managed, serverless solution.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use an LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate its faithfulness. Which of the following is the best prompt to use for the judge LLM?
answers: 'Is this a good answer?'
'Does the answer contain any hallucinations?'
'Given the following context and the following answer, is the answer fully supported by the information in the context? Answer with only 'yes' or 'no'.'
'Please rewrite the answer to be more faithful.'
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is too vague and does not specifically ask about faithfulness.
Incorrect: This is a leading question and is not the most objective way to frame the task.
Correct: This is a clear, a concise, and an objective prompt that frames the task as a simple verification problem. This is the standard way to prompt an LLM-as-a-judge for a faithfulness evaluation.
Incorrect: The goal of the evaluation is to assess the faithfulness of the existing answer, not to generate a new one.
questions.explanation: When you are using an LLM as a judge, the quality of your prompt is critical. For a faithfulness evaluation, you want a prompt that is clear, is objective, and that frames the task in a way that is easy for the LLM to understand. The best practice is to provide the LLM with the retrieved context and the generated answer, and to ask it a simple, direct question: 'Is the answer fully supported by the context?' By also constraining the output to be a simple 'yes' or 'no', you can make the evaluation process even more reliable and easy to parse.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to follow MLOps best practices. Which TWO of the following are the most important reasons to use a CI/CD pipeline for the application?
answers: To make the deployment process faster and more reliable.
To ensure that every change to the application is automatically tested before it is deployed.
To allow developers to deploy to production without getting any approvals.
To make it more difficult for new developers to contribute to the project.
feedbacks: Correct: Automation through CI/CD eliminates the manual, error-prone steps of the deployment process, which makes it much faster and much more reliable.
Correct: Automated testing is a key part of a CI/CD pipeline. It provides a crucial safety net that helps to prevent bugs from reaching production.
Incorrect: A good CI/CD pipeline will often have an approval step for the deployment to production. The goal of the pipeline is to automate the process, not to eliminate the governance.
Incorrect: A good CI/CD pipeline should make it easier, not harder, for new developers to contribute, as it provides a clear and an automated path to production.
questions.explanation: A CI/CD pipeline is a fundamental MLOps best practice that provides two key benefits: speed and safety. By automating the deployment process, a CI/CD pipeline can significantly reduce the time it takes to get a new version of the application into production. By including a comprehensive set of automated tests in the pipeline, it can also significantly improve the safety and the reliability of the deployment process. This combination of speed and safety is what allows teams to iterate quickly and to deliver value to their users in a reliable and a consistent way.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that are very specific and that require finding a small piece of information in a large document. Which of the following chunking strategies would be most effective?
answers: Using a very large chunk size.
Using a small chunk size, with a good amount of overlap.

Using a chunking strategy that creates a hierarchy of chunks, for example, by creating chunks for each section, each paragraph, and each sentence. The retriever could then search over the smallest chunks.
Combining the entire document into a single chunk.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A large chunk size would make it harder to find a small, specific piece of information, as the signal would be diluted by all the other information in the chunk.

Correct: For extractive tasks, a smaller chunk size is often better. It allows the retriever to find a very specific and a very focused piece of text. The overlap is important to ensure that a piece of information that spans a chunk boundary is not lost.

Correct: This is a very powerful, hierarchical approach. By creating chunks at multiple levels of granularity, you can allow the retriever to 'zoom in' to find the most specific and the most relevant piece of information.
Incorrect: This would be the worst possible strategy for this use case.
questions.explanation: When the goal is to find a small, specific needle in a large haystack of a document, your chunking strategy needs to be designed for precision. The two best ways to achieve this are to use a small chunk size or to use a hierarchical chunking strategy. A small chunk size creates a very fine-grained index of your document, which makes it easier for the retriever to find a very specific passage. A hierarchical chunking strategy is an even more powerful approach. It allows the retriever to first find the right section of the document, and then to 'zoom in' to find the right paragraph or the right sentence. Both of these strategies are much more effective for extractive question-answering than a strategy that uses large chunks.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to monitor its performance. They have set up logging to an inference table. Which of the following is the most important piece of information to include in the logs for each request, to enable effective debugging and analysis?
answers: The IP address of the user.
A unique 'trace ID' that can be used to correlate the request with all the downstream operations that were performed to generate the response.
The name of the developer who wrote the code for the RAG chain.
The time of day that the request was made.
feedbacks: Incorrect: For privacy reasons, you should generally avoid logging the user's IP address unless you have a specific and a compliant reason to do so.

Correct: A trace ID is absolutely essential for debugging a complex, distributed system like a RAG application. It allows you to follow a single request as it flows through all the different components of the system.
Incorrect: This is not relevant information for the logs.

Correct: A timestamp is another essential piece of information. It's needed for calculating latency, for tracking performance over time, and for correlating the request with other events in the system.
questions.explanation: High-quality logging is the foundation of a good monitoring and a good debugging strategy. For a RAG application, the two most important pieces of information to include in your logs for each request are a unique trace ID and a timestamp. The trace ID is what allows you to tie together all the different events that are associated with a single request, which is essential for debugging. The timestamp is what allows you to understand the performance of your system and to analyze trends over time. With just these two pieces of information, you can build a very powerful and a very effective monitoring solution.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that its development process is as efficient as possible. Which TWO of the following Databricks features are most helpful for accelerating the 'inner loop' of the development process (i.e., the code-run-debug cycle)?
answers: The Databricks Jobs scheduler.
Databricks Notebooks, which provide an interactive environment for writing and for running code.
The AI Playground, which allows for the quick, interactive testing of different models and prompts.
The Unity Catalog data explorer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The job scheduler is for running production jobs, not for the interactive development process.
Correct: The interactive nature of Databricks Notebooks is perfect for the rapid, iterative development that is common in data science and AI.
Correct: The AI Playground is a powerful tool for accelerating the prompt engineering and the model selection part of the development process.
Incorrect: The data explorer is for browsing data, not for developing code.
questions.explanation: The 'inner loop' of development is all about the speed at which a developer can write code, can run it, and can see the results. Databricks provides two key features that are designed to make this loop as fast and as efficient as possible. The first is the interactive notebook environment, which allows developers to write and to execute code in small, incremental steps. The second is the AI Playground, which is a purpose-built UI for interactively experimenting with different LLMs and different prompts. By using these two tools together, a developer can very quickly iterate on their RAG application and can find the best combination of code, prompts, and models.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions about a product's inventory, which is stored in a real-time database. Which of the following is the best architecture for this?
answers: A RAG chain that has the entire inventory database converted to a text file and stored in its knowledge base.
A LangChain agent that has a tool for querying the real-time inventory database.
A RAG system that is fine-tuned on historical inventory data.
A RAG system that asks the user to go and to check the inventory database themselves.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be a static solution and would not provide real-time information.
Correct: This is the perfect architecture for this use case. The agent can use the tool to get the up-to-the-minute inventory information whenever a user asks a question about it.
Incorrect: This would not provide real-time information.
Incorrect: This would not be a very helpful application.
questions.explanation: When a RAG application needs to access real-time data from an external system, an agent-based architecture with a tool is the best solution. The tool would encapsulate the logic for connecting to the real-time database and for querying the inventory for a specific product. The agent would then be able to use this tool to get the live, up-to-the-minute information that it needs to answer the user's question. This is a much more powerful and a much more flexible approach than trying to work with a static copy of the data.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is simple and is easy to understand. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Semantic chunking.
Fixed-size chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Sentence-level chunking.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the most complex chunking strategy.
Correct: This is the simplest possible chunking strategy. You just split the text every N characters.
Incorrect: While a very good strategy, it is more complex than simple fixed-size or sentence-level chunking.
Correct: Splitting the text by sentences is also a very simple and a very easy-to-understand strategy.
questions.explanation: When simplicity is the top priority for a chunking strategy, the two best choices are fixed-size chunking and sentence-level chunking. Fixed-size chunking is the absolute simplest approach, and it can be a surprisingly effective baseline for many applications. Sentence-level chunking is also very simple and has the added benefit of respecting the natural semantic boundaries of the text. For many use cases, one of these two simple strategies is all that is needed to get good results.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to evaluate it. They have a golden dataset of question-answer pairs. Which TWO of the following are the most important quality metrics that they can measure with this dataset?
answers: The latency of the application.
The correctness of the generated answers, as compared to the golden answers.
The user satisfaction with the answers.
The semantic similarity between the generated answers and the golden answers.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a performance metric, not a quality metric that requires a golden dataset.
