Converting the documents to plain text and then using a sentence-based chunking strategy.
Using a recursive character text splitter with separators defined based on the numbering and headings of the clauses and sub-clauses.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would almost certainly break up the legal clauses in a way that would make them incomprehensible.
Correct: For highly structured and domain-specific documents like legal contracts, a custom, content-aware chunking strategy is often the only way to get high-quality results.
Incorrect: This would lose the critical structural information of the contracts.

Correct: This is another excellent approach for structured documents. By defining the separators based on the legal numbering scheme (e.g., 'Section 1.1', 'Article II'), you can create chunks that align perfectly with the logical structure of the contract.
questions.explanation: Legal contracts are a prime example of documents where the structure is just as important as the text itself. A naive chunking strategy would be disastrous. The two best approaches are to use a custom, content-aware chunking script or to use a recursive character text splitter that is configured to understand the specific structure of the documents. A custom script can be very powerful if the structure of the contracts is consistent. It can be written to parse the document and to extract each clause and sub-clause as a separate, semantically complete unit. A recursive character text splitter can achieve a similar result in a more declarative way, by defining the separators based on the patterns used in the contract's headings and numbering. Both of these approaches will produce much higher-quality chunks than any generic method.

questions.question: A team is evaluating their RAG application and wants to get a qualitative understanding of its failure modes. Which of the following is the most effective way to do this?
answers: Calculating the average ROUGE score across a large test set.

Performing an error analysis, where they manually review a set of failed cases and categorize the types of errors (e.g., 'retrieved irrelevant document', 'hallucinated answer', 'misinterpreted question').
Measuring the end-to-end latency of the application.
Asking the LLM to explain why it generated a particular answer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While ROUGE scores are useful for quantitative evaluation, they don't provide a qualitative understanding of the types of errors the system is making.

Correct: Error analysis is a fundamental part of the machine learning development cycle. By manually inspecting the failures, the team can gain a deep, qualitative understanding of where the system is going wrong, which is essential for being able to fix it.
Incorrect: Latency is a performance metric, not a measure of the types of errors.
Incorrect: While this can sometimes be useful for debugging a single case, it's not a systematic way to understand the overall failure modes of the application.
questions.explanation: Quantitative metrics are important, but they don't tell the whole story. To truly understand why a RAG application is failing, you need to do a qualitative error analysis. This involves taking a sample of the cases where the application produced a poor result and manually examining them to understand the root cause of the failure. By categorizing the errors (e.g., retrieval errors, generation errors, etc.), the team can identify the main weaknesses of their system and can then prioritize their efforts to fix them. This qualitative feedback loop is just as important as the quantitative one for building a high-quality application.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain application and wants to create a prompt template that can be used with different LLMs, some of which use different variable syntaxes (e.g., `{{variable}}` vs. `{variable}`). Which of the following is the best way to handle this?
answers: Creating a separate prompt template for each LLM.
Using the `PromptTemplate` class and letting it handle the variable formatting automatically.
Writing a custom function to replace the variables in the prompt string.
Not using any variables in the prompt and just hardcoding all the text.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be duplicative and difficult to maintain.

Correct: The LangChain `PromptTemplate` class is designed to be flexible. You can define your template with a consistent syntax (e.g., `{variable}`), and LangChain will handle the necessary formatting when the prompt is used with a specific LLM.
Incorrect: This is unnecessary, as LangChain provides this functionality out-of-the-box.
Incorrect: This would make the prompt static and not reusable.
questions.explanation: LangChain is designed to be a flexible and interoperable framework. The `PromptTemplate` class abstracts away the details of the specific variable syntax used by different LLMs. You can define your prompt template using a standard Python f-string-like syntax (e.g., `'Answer the following question: {question}'`), and LangChain will automatically adapt this to the format expected by the LLM you are using. This makes it easy to write portable prompt templates that can be used with a variety of different models.

questions.question: A data engineer is preparing a dataset of text documents for a RAG application. The documents are from a variety of sources and are in different file formats (PDF, Word, HTML). Which of the following is the best first step in the data preparation pipeline?
answers: Trying to create embeddings directly from the raw files.
Using a document parsing library that can handle multiple file formats and can extract the clean text from each document.
Manually converting all the files to a single format, such as plain text.
Choosing to only support a single file format and ignoring the others.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Embedding models work on plain text, not on the raw bytes of a file.

Correct: A good document parsing library (like Unstructured.io) is essential for a RAG pipeline that needs to handle multiple file formats. It can abstract away the complexity of dealing with each file type and can provide a consistent, clean text output.
Incorrect: This would be a very time-consuming and manual process.
Incorrect: This would limit the knowledge base of the RAG application and would not meet the requirement of using all the documents.
questions.explanation: When you have to deal with a variety of document formats, the first and most important step is to use a robust document parsing library. Libraries like Unstructured.io are designed for this exact purpose. They can take a variety of file types as input (PDF, Word, HTML, etc.) and can produce a clean, consistent plain text output. This abstracts away the complexity of handling each file format individually and provides a solid foundation for the rest of your RAG data preparation pipeline (chunking, embedding, etc.).

questions.question: A team is evaluating their RAG application and wants to use an LLM to help with the evaluation. For example, they want to use an LLM to judge whether a generated answer is faithful to the retrieved context. This technique is known as:
answers: LLM-as-a-critic.
LLM-as-a-judge.
LLM-as-a-teacher.
LLM-as-a-student.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this term is sometimes used, 'LLM-as-a-judge' is the more common and accepted term.

Correct: 'LLM-as-a-judge' is the term used to describe the technique of using a powerful LLM (like GPT-4) to evaluate the output of another LLM. This can be a very effective and scalable way to perform evaluation. [31]
Incorrect: This term is not typically used in the context of evaluation.
Incorrect: This term is not typically used in the context of evaluation.
questions.explanation: 'LLM-as-a-judge' is a powerful and increasingly popular technique for evaluating generative AI applications. [31] The idea is to use a capable LLM (often a large and powerful one like GPT-4) as an impartial 'judge' to score the output of the LLM being tested. You can provide the judge LLM with a rubric and a set of criteria (e.g., 'is the answer faithful to the context?', 'is the answer relevant to the question?'), and it can then provide a score and a rationale for its evaluation. This can be a much more scalable and cost-effective approach than relying solely on human evaluation.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application that is used by a team of customer support agents. They want to provide the agents with a way to give feedback on the quality of the answers they are receiving. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO of the most effective ways to collect this feedback?
answers: A 'thumbs up' / 'thumbs down' button next to each answer.
A complex, multi-page survey that the agents have to fill out at the end of each day.
An optional free-text field where the agent can provide a short explanation for their rating.
Requiring the agents to send an email to the development team every time they get a bad answer.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a simple and low-friction way for users to provide a quick signal on the quality of the answer.
Incorrect: This would be too time-consuming and would likely lead to low engagement.
Correct: Combining a simple rating system (like thumbs up/down) with an optional text field is a great way to collect both quantitative and qualitative feedback.
Incorrect: This would be an unstructured and inefficient way to collect feedback.
questions.explanation: Collecting user feedback is crucial for improving a RAG application. The key is to make the feedback process as easy and low-friction as possible. A simple 'thumbs up' / 'thumbs down' button is a great way to get a quick, quantitative signal on the quality of each answer. To get more detailed, qualitative feedback, you can then add an optional free-text field where the user can explain *why* they gave a particular rating. This combination of a simple rating and an optional text box provides a rich source of feedback that is invaluable for the development team, without placing a heavy burden on the users.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions based on information from both a structured database and a collection of unstructured documents. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO of the most effective architectures for this type of hybrid RAG system?
answers: A RAG system that only uses the unstructured documents and ignores the structured database.

An agent-based system where the LLM is given two tools: one for querying the database (a 'query' tool) and one for searching the documents (a 'retrieval' tool). The agent can then decide which tool to use based on the user's question.
A system that first converts the entire structured database into a set of unstructured documents and then performs retrieval over the combined set of documents.
A RAG chain that first retrieves relevant documents and then, in a second step, uses the information from those documents to generate a SQL query to run against the database.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not meet the requirement of using both data sources.
Correct: An agent-based approach is very flexible and is well-suited for hybrid RAG. The agent can intelligently route the user's query to the appropriate data source.
Incorrect: This would lose the valuable structure of the database and would be very inefficient.
Correct: This is another valid and powerful pattern. The unstructured documents can provide the context that the LLM needs to be able to generate an accurate and relevant SQL query.
questions.explanation: When you need to build a RAG application that works over both structured and unstructured data, you need to design a system that can leverage the strengths of both. The two most effective architectures for this are an agent-based system and a multi-step RAG chain. The agent-based approach is very flexible, as the LLM can decide on-the-fly whether to query the database or the document store. The multi-step chain approach is also very powerful, especially for queries that require context from the documents to be able to correctly query the database. The choice between these two architectures will depend on the specific requirements of the application.

questions.question: A team is preparing a dataset of meeting transcripts for a RAG application. The transcripts include the names of the speakers for each turn in the conversation. What is the most effective way to include this speaker information in the data that is chunked and embedded?
answers: Removing the speaker names to create a more uniform text.
Keeping the speaker names in the text, for example by prefixing each line with 'Speaker A:' or 'Speaker B:'.
Creating a separate metadata field for the speaker for each chunk.
Replacing all speaker names with a generic token like '[SPEAKER]'.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The speaker information is a critical piece of context and should be preserved.
Correct: This is the most direct and effective way to preserve the speaker information. It provides clear context to the embedding model and the LLM about who said what.

Correct: This is another excellent approach. Most vector databases allow you to store metadata alongside the vectors. You could store the speaker's name as metadata, which would then allow you to filter your search results based on the speaker.
Incorrect: This would lose the specific information about which speaker said what.
questions.explanation: When working with conversational data like meeting transcripts, preserving the speaker information is crucial. There are two primary ways to do this effectively. The first is to include the speaker names directly in the text that gets embedded. This provides direct, in-band context to the models. The second, and often more powerful, way is to store the speaker information as a metadata field in the vector database. This not only preserves the information but also turns it into a powerful tool for retrieval. For example, a user could then ask a question like, 'What did John say about the marketing budget?', and the RAG system could use the metadata to specifically retrieve only the chunks of text that were spoken by John.

questions.question: A team has deployed a RAG application to production and wants to set up automated alerts to notify them if the quality of the application's responses starts to degrade. Which TWO of the following are the most effective ways to do this on Databricks?
answers: Manually checking a sample of the application's responses each day.

Using Databricks Lakehouse Monitoring to track key quality metrics (like faithfulness or answer relevancy, as calculated by an LLM-as-a-judge model) and to set up alerts that trigger when these metrics fall below a certain threshold.
Asking users to send an email to the team if they are not happy with an answer.

Creating a Databricks SQL Alert that runs a query against the inference tables to check for an increase in the number of 'thumbs down' ratings (assuming such a feedback mechanism is in place and is logged).
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not an automated or scalable solution.
Correct: Lakehouse Monitoring is designed for this exact purpose. It can track metrics over time and can be configured to send alerts when it detects a problem.
Incorrect: While user feedback is valuable, it is not a reliable or comprehensive way to monitor the overall quality of the system.

Correct: If you are logging user feedback to your inference tables, you can use Databricks SQL Alerts to create a powerful and responsive monitoring system. An alert can run a query on a schedule and can notify the team if it detects a spike in negative feedback.
questions.explanation: Automated monitoring and alerting are essential for maintaining the quality of a production RAG application. On Databricks, there are two excellent ways to achieve this. The first is to use Databricks Lakehouse Monitoring. This is a managed solution that can track a wide variety of metrics, including custom metrics calculated by an LLM-as-a-judge, and can automatically send alerts when there is a problem. The second approach is to use Databricks SQL Alerts. This is a very flexible solution that allows you to write a SQL query against any of your data (such as the inference tables) and to trigger an alert based on the results of that query. Both of these methods provide a robust and automated way to stay on top of the quality of your RAG application.

questions.question: A developer is building a complex LangChain agent that involves multiple tools and a lot of conditional logic. They are finding it difficult to debug the agent's behavior. Which of the following is the most effective tool for debugging and tracing the execution of a LangChain agent?
answers: Using a series of `print()` statements throughout the agent's code.
LangSmith.
MLflow.
The Python debugger (`pdb`).
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this can be helpful for simple scripts, it's not an effective way to debug a complex, asynchronous agent.

Correct: LangSmith is a platform built by LangChain that is specifically designed for the debugging, tracing, and evaluation of LLM applications. It provides a detailed, visual trace of the agent's execution, which makes it much easier to understand and to debug.
Incorrect: While MLflow is great for overall MLOps, LangSmith is the specialized tool for the inner loop of developing and debugging LangChain applications.
Incorrect: While a powerful tool, `pdb` can be difficult to use with the asynchronous and callback-based nature of many LangChain agents. LangSmith provides a much more intuitive experience.
questions.explanation: For anyone building complex applications with LangChain, LangSmith is an indispensable tool. It's designed to give you full visibility into the execution of your chains and agents. For any given run, LangSmith will show you a detailed trace of all the steps involved: the inputs and outputs of each LLM call, the tools that were used, and the full context at each step. This level of detail is invaluable for debugging complex behaviors and for understanding why your agent is not behaving as expected.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a set of documents that are already well-structured and have been chunked into meaningful sections. They now need to create embeddings for these chunks. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO important considerations for this embedding generation step?
answers: Choosing an embedding model that is appropriate for the domain and the language of the documents.
Using the most powerful and expensive embedding model available, regardless of the cost.
Deciding on a batch size for the embedding process to balance performance and memory usage.
Combining all the chunks into a single document before creating the embedding.
feedbacks: Correct: The choice of embedding model is critical. A model that is well-suited to the language and the specific domain of your documents will produce much more meaningful embeddings.
Incorrect: There is often a trade-off between performance and cost, and the most expensive model is not always necessary.

Correct: When creating embeddings for a large number of chunks, you need to process them in batches. The size of the batch will affect the overall speed of the process and the amount of memory required.
Incorrect: This would defeat the purpose of chunking and would result in a single, meaningless embedding for the entire dataset.
questions.explanation: Once you have your text chunks, the next critical step is to create high-quality embeddings. Two of the most important considerations for this are choosing the right model and choosing the right batch size. The embedding model you choose should be well-suited to your data. For example, if your documents are in a language other than English, you'll need a multilingual model. If your documents are from a specialized domain, you might consider a fine-tuned model. The batch size is a more practical consideration, but it's still important. It affects the performance of the embedding process, and you'll need to choose a size that makes efficient use of your hardware (especially if you are using a GPU) without running out of memory.

questions.question: A company is preparing to deploy a new RAG application and has created a 'golden dataset' of question-answer pairs for evaluation. Which TWO of the following metrics can be calculated using this golden dataset?
answers: Contextual Relevance.
Answer Correctness, where an LLM or a human evaluates whether the generated answer is semantically equivalent to the golden answer.
Latency.
Semantic Similarity between the generated answer and the golden answer, as calculated by an embedding model.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Contextual Relevance is typically calculated without a golden dataset, often by using an LLM-as-a-judge.
Correct: When you have a golden answer, you can use it as a reference to evaluate the correctness of the generated answer.
Incorrect: Latency is a performance metric and does not require a golden dataset.

Correct: You can use an embedding model to calculate the semantic similarity between the generated answer and the golden answer. A high similarity score would indicate that the generated answer is close in meaning to the ideal answer.
questions.explanation: A 'golden dataset' of question-answer pairs is a powerful asset for evaluating a RAG application. Two of the key metrics that you can calculate with such a dataset are Answer Correctness and Semantic Similarity. Answer Correctness involves comparing the generated answer to the golden answer to see if it is factually correct and contains all the necessary information. This comparison can be done by a human evaluator or by a powerful LLM-as-a-judge. Semantic Similarity is a more automated approach, where you use an embedding model to compute the similarity between the vector representations of the generated answer and the golden answer. A high score on this metric indicates that the two answers are semantically close.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by thousands of concurrent users. Which of the following is the most scalable and cost-effective architecture for deploying this application on Databricks?
answers: Deploying the application as a job on a large, always-on Databricks cluster.
Using Databricks Model Serving for the LLM and the RAG chain, with auto-scaling enabled.
Using Databricks Vector Search for the retrieval component.
Running the application in a Databricks notebook and using the 'Run All' button for each user query.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be as scalable or as cost-effective as using a dedicated serving solution.
Correct: Model Serving is designed for high-throughput, low-latency inference and its auto-scaling capability makes it both scalable and cost-effective.
Correct: Vector Search is a serverless, highly scalable vector database that is ideal for production RAG applications with a large number of users.
Incorrect: This is not a scalable or a production-ready solution.
questions.explanation: For a high-concurrency, production-grade RAG application on Databricks, the ideal architecture leverages the platform's serverless and auto-scaling capabilities. For the retrieval component, Databricks Vector Search provides a fully managed and highly scalable vector database that can handle a large number of queries. For the generation component, Databricks Model Serving provides a robust and efficient way to deploy the RAG chain and the LLM. By enabling auto-scaling on the serving endpoint, the system can automatically adjust its capacity to meet the fluctuating demand, ensuring both high performance and cost-effectiveness.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that are sensitive to the time the question is asked. For example, 'What was the stock price of company X yesterday?' Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO key components of a RAG system that can handle this kind of time-sensitive query?
answers: An LLM that has been fine-tuned on historical stock price data.
A data pipeline that continuously ingests and updates the knowledge base with the latest information.
An agent-based architecture where the LLM has access to a real-time data API as a tool.
A prompt that asks the LLM to 'please provide the most recent information'.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Fine-tuning is on a static dataset and would not provide access to yesterday's stock price.
Correct: To answer questions about recent events, the RAG system's knowledge base must be kept up-to-date. This requires a robust and continuous data pipeline.

Correct: For truly up-to-the-minute information, the best approach is to give the agent a tool that can query a real-time API. For the stock price example, this would be an API to a financial data provider.
Incorrect: The LLM cannot access real-time information on its own, so this prompt would not be effective.
questions.explanation: Handling time-sensitive queries is a common challenge for RAG applications. The key to solving this is to ensure that the system has access to up-to-date information. There are two main ways to achieve this. The first is to have a continuous data pipeline that is always updating the knowledge base (e.g., the Delta tables and the vector index) with the latest data. This is a good approach for data that changes frequently but not necessarily in real-time. The second, and more powerful, approach is to use an agent-based architecture where the LLM has access to a tool that can query a real-time API. This allows the agent to get the absolute latest information at the time the query is asked, which is essential for use cases like checking stock prices or news updates.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a set of documents that are very long. They are concerned that if they create chunks that are too long, they will exceed the context window of the LLM. Which TWO of the following are the most effective strategies to deal with this?
answers: Using a smaller LLM with a larger context window.
Using a text splitter that allows you to set a maximum chunk size, and also has an overlap between chunks.
Summarizing the long documents first, and then chunking the summaries.
Simply truncating the documents to fit within the context window.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A smaller LLM is likely to have a smaller, not a larger, context window.

Correct: A text splitter with a configurable max size and overlap is the standard way to handle this. The max size ensures you don't exceed the context window, and the overlap helps to preserve context at the chunk boundaries.

Correct: This is a powerful, advanced technique known as 'summarize-then-retrieve'. It can be very effective for very long documents, as it allows you to create a more condensed representation of the document that still captures the key information.
Incorrect: This would result in a significant loss of information.
questions.explanation: Dealing with very long documents is a common challenge in RAG. The two most effective strategies are to use a smart chunking strategy and to use a summarization pre-processing step. A good text splitter will allow you to set a hard limit on the chunk size to ensure that you don't exceed the LLM's context window, while the overlap feature helps to mitigate the loss of context at the split points. An even more advanced technique is to first use an LLM to summarize the long document (or large sections of it) and then to perform the RAG process on these summaries. This can be a very effective way to distill the key information from a long document into a more manageable size.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use MLflow to manage the lifecycle of the application. Which TWO of the following are valid ways to use MLflow in the context of a RAG application?
answers: Using MLflow Tracking to log and compare experiments with different prompts, embedding models, and LLMs.
Using MLflow as a real-time vector database.
Using the MLflow Model Registry to version and manage the final, packaged RAG chain as a deployable model.
Using MLflow to write the data preparation pipeline for the RAG application.
feedbacks: Correct: MLflow Tracking is ideal for the iterative development process of a RAG application, allowing you to systematically test different components and to find the best combination.
Incorrect: MLflow is not a vector database.
Correct: You can log the entire RAG chain as an MLflow model and then use the Model Registry to manage its lifecycle, for example, by promoting it from staging to production.
Incorrect: MLflow is not a data pipeline tool. You would use a tool like Delta Live Tables for that.
questions.explanation: MLflow is a critical component of the MLOps for RAG workflow on Databricks. It plays a key role in two main areas: experimentation and lifecycle management. During the development phase, MLflow Tracking is used to log all the details of your experiments, allowing you to compare different approaches and to find the best-performing model. Once you have a RAG chain that you are happy with, you can log the entire chain as an MLflow model and then use the MLflow Model Registry to manage its lifecycle. This provides a robust, versioned, and auditable way to move your RAG application from development to production.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to use an open-source vector database that they can host themselves. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO popular and valid open-source choices for this?
answers: Databricks Vector Search.
Chroma DB.
Pinecone.
Weaviate.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Databricks Vector Search is a proprietary, managed service, not an open-source, self-hosted database.
Correct: Chroma DB is a popular, open-source vector database that is easy to get started with and can be self-hosted.
Incorrect: Pinecone is a proprietary, managed vector database service.
Correct: Weaviate is another popular and powerful open-source vector database that can be self-hosted and offers a rich set of features.
questions.explanation: For teams that want the flexibility and control of a self-hosted, open-source vector database, there are several excellent choices available. Two of the most popular and well-regarded are Chroma DB and Weaviate. Chroma DB is known for its simplicity and ease of use, making it a great choice for getting started and for smaller projects. Weaviate is a more feature-rich and powerful option, with capabilities like hybrid search and advanced filtering, making it a good choice for more demanding, production applications. Both are strong open-source alternatives to managed services like Databricks Vector Search or Pinecone.

questions.question: A developer is working with a LangChain chain and wants to be able to easily switch between different LLMs (e.g., from OpenAI, Anthropic, and a self-hosted model) without changing the rest of their code. This is an example of which key software engineering principle that LangChain's design facilitates?
answers: Inheritance.
Abstraction.
Encapsulation.
Polymorphism.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While LangChain uses object-oriented principles, the key principle at play here is abstraction.

Correct: LangChain provides a common `LLM` abstraction (or more recently, the `ChatModel` abstraction) that has a standardized interface. This allows you to write your code against this common interface, and then you can easily swap out the specific implementation (e.g., `OpenAI`, `ChatAnthropic`) without changing the rest of your application logic.
Incorrect: While related to object-oriented design, abstraction is the more specific principle that applies here.

Correct: This is another correct answer that describes the same concept from a different object-oriented perspective. The ability to use different LLM objects through the same interface is a classic example of polymorphism.
questions.explanation: A key design goal of LangChain is to provide a set of standard, high-level abstractions for the common components of an LLM application. The `LLM` and `ChatModel` classes are prime examples of this. By providing a common interface for interacting with different language models, LangChain allows developers to write code that is not tied to a specific model provider. This makes it easy to switch between different models for experimentation or to move from a proprietary model to a self-hosted one without having to rewrite the entire application. This is a classic example of the power of abstraction and polymorphism in software engineering.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that are full of acronyms. They want to ensure that the RAG system can correctly understand these acronyms. Which TWO of the following are the most effective strategies for handling this?
answers: Removing all the acronyms from the text.
Creating a pre-processing step that expands the acronyms, for example, by replacing 'RAG' with 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation'.
Fine-tuning the embedding model and the LLM on a version of the documents where the acronyms have been expanded.
Ignoring the acronyms and hoping that the LLM will understand them from the context.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would remove important information from the documents.
Correct: By expanding the acronyms, you make the text much more explicit and easier for the embedding model and the LLM to understand.

Correct: This is a more advanced but very powerful technique. By fine-tuning the models on the expanded text, you can teach them the meaning of the acronyms within the specific domain, which can lead to a significant improvement in performance.
Incorrect: While LLMs are good at understanding context, they can still make mistakes with ambiguous or domain-specific acronyms. It's better to be explicit.
questions.explanation: Acronyms can be a major source of ambiguity for a RAG system. The best way to handle them is to make their meaning explicit. The two most effective strategies for this are to expand them in a pre-processing step and to fine-tune the models on the expanded text. A pre-processing step that replaces the acronyms with their full definitions is a straightforward and often very effective way to improve the quality of the data. For even better performance, you can fine-tune the embedding model and the LLM on this expanded text. This will help the models to internalize the meaning of the acronyms and to better understand the nuances of the domain-specific language.

questions.question: A company is preparing to launch a new RAG application and wants to have a clear plan for evaluating it. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO of the key dimensions of quality that should be evaluated for a RAG application?
answers: The programming language that the application is written in.
The performance of the retrieval component (e.g., as measured by metrics like contextual precision and recall).
The quality of the generation component (e.g., as measured by metrics like faithfulness and answer relevancy).
The number of lines of code in the application.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The programming language is an implementation detail and not a dimension of the application's quality.
Correct: The quality of the retrieved documents is a critical factor in the overall performance of a RAG system.
Correct: The quality of the final generated answer is the other critical dimension of a RAG system's performance.
Incorrect: This is not a measure of the application's quality.
questions.explanation: A RAG system can be thought of as having two main components: the retriever and the generator. A comprehensive evaluation plan must therefore assess the quality of both of these components. The quality of the retrieval component is all about whether the system is finding the right information. This is typically measured with metrics like contextual precision and contextual recall. The quality of the generation component is all about whether the system is using that information correctly to generate a good answer. This is typically measured with metrics like faithfulness and answer relevancy. A high-quality RAG application must perform well on both of these dimensions.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that all the Python libraries and dependencies used in the application are managed and versioned consistently. Which TWO of the following are the best ways to achieve this on Databricks?
answers: Having each developer on the team install the libraries they need on their own local machine.
Specifying the required libraries in the cluster configuration for the development and production clusters.
Using a `%pip install` command in the first cell of every notebook.
Using a requirements.txt or a pyproject.toml file to define the dependencies and then using MLflow Projects or Databricks Repos to manage the project and its dependencies.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would lead to inconsistencies and the 'it works on my machine' problem.
Correct: You can specify the libraries to be installed on a Databricks cluster, which ensures that all code running on that cluster uses the same set of dependencies.
Incorrect: While this can be used for quick experiments, it's not a good practice for production code, as it makes it harder to manage dependencies consistently.
Correct: This is a best practice for Python development in general and is fully supported on Databricks. It provides a declarative and version-controlled way to manage your dependencies.
questions.explanation: Consistent and version-controlled dependency management is crucial for building reliable and reproducible applications. On Databricks, there are two main best practices for this. The first is to specify the required libraries in the cluster configuration. This is a simple and effective way to ensure that everyone working on a particular project is using the same set of dependencies. The second, and more robust, approach is to use a standard Python dependency management file like `requirements.txt`. This file can be checked into a version control system (like a Databricks Repo) and then used to install the correct dependencies on any cluster where the code is run. This is a key part of the MLflow Projects workflow and is a best practice for any production Python project.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and has found that for some questions, the LLM provides a correct answer but in a very verbose and unhelpful way. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO prompt engineering techniques that could be used to make the LLM's responses more concise and to the point?
answers: Asking the LLM to 'be as detailed as possible'.
Providing a few-shot example in the prompt that shows a concise and well-formatted answer.
Adding an instruction to the prompt such as 'Answer in a single sentence' or 'Provide a bulleted list of the key points'.
Using a more powerful and capable LLM.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would likely make the response even more verbose.
Correct: By showing the LLM an example of what you want, you can often guide it to produce a similar output.
Correct: Giving the LLM explicit constraints on the length or format of its response is a very effective way to make it more concise.
Incorrect: A more powerful LLM might still be verbose if not given the right instructions.
questions.explanation: Controlling the verbosity and format of an LLM's output is a common challenge in prompt engineering. Two of the most effective techniques for this are to use few-shot examples and to provide explicit constraints in the prompt. By including a few examples of concise, well-formatted answers in your prompt, you can show the LLM exactly what you are looking for. By adding explicit instructions, such as 'keep the answer to under 50 words' or 'respond with a yes or no', you can directly control the output of the model. A combination of these two techniques is often the most effective way to get the LLM to produce responses that are both accurate and concise.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that contain many tables. They want to ensure that the information in these tables is effectively used by the RAG system. Which TWO of the following are the most effective strategies for handling these tables?
answers: Converting the tables to images and using an image embedding model.
Extracting the tables from the documents and converting them to a structured format like CSV or Markdown.
Representing each table as a 'create table' SQL statement, followed by a set of 'insert' statements.
Ignoring the tables and only using the surrounding text.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be a very indirect and likely ineffective way to handle the structured information in the tables.
Correct: The first step is to get the tables out of the documents and into a structured format that preserves their rows and columns.

Correct: This is a powerful and increasingly popular technique. By representing the table as a SQL schema, you make it very easy for the LLM to understand the structure and the content of the table, and to potentially even query it.
Incorrect: The tables often contain the most important information in a document.
questions.explanation: Tables are a rich source of information, but they can be challenging for RAG systems. The key is to represent them in a way that an LLM can understand. The two most effective ways to do this are to convert them to a simple structured format like Markdown, or to represent them as SQL statements. Converting a table to a Markdown table is a simple and often effective way to preserve its structure in a text-based format. A more advanced and powerful technique is to represent the table as a 'CREATE TABLE' statement (to define the schema) and a set of 'INSERT' statements (to provide the data). This format is very natural for an LLM that has been trained on a lot of code, and it makes it very easy for the model to understand the structure and content of the table.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and is using a 'thumbs up' / 'thumbs down' feedback mechanism to collect user ratings on the answers. They have logged this feedback to their inference tables. They now want to create a daily report that shows the percentage of 'thumbs up' ratings. Which of the following is the best tool on Databricks to automate the generation of this report?
answers: A Databricks Notebook that queries the inference table and calculates the metric, scheduled to run as a daily job.
Databricks Model Serving.
Unity Catalog.
Manually running a query in the SQL editor each day.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a straightforward and effective way to automate the report generation. You can use PySpark or SQL to query the data and then use the job scheduler to run the notebook every day.
Incorrect: Model Serving is for deploying models, not for running data reports.
Incorrect: Unity Catalog is for data governance, not for running reports.
Incorrect: This is not an automated solution.
questions.explanation: Databricks provides a powerful and flexible platform for automating data reporting. For the use case of generating a daily report on user feedback, the best approach is to create a Databricks Notebook that contains the logic for querying the inference table and calculating the required metric. This notebook can then be scheduled to run as a daily job using the Databricks Jobs scheduler. This provides a fully automated, reliable, and scalable way to generate the report. The output of the job could be a new Delta table with the daily metrics, which could then be used to power a dashboard or to send out an email report.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to use a managed, serverless vector database that is deeply integrated with their Databricks environment. Which of the following is the best choice for them?
answers: Chroma DB, deployed on a separate virtual machine.
Databricks Vector Search.
FAISS, running in a Databricks notebook.
Elasticsearch with the vector search plugin, running on a separate cluster.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be a managed, serverless, or deeply integrated solution.
Correct: Databricks Vector Search is the native, fully managed, and serverless vector database on the Databrisck platform. It is designed for deep integration with the rest of the ecosystem.
Incorrect: While you can use FAISS in a notebook, it is not a managed, serverless database solution.
Incorrect: This would be a self-managed solution and would not be as deeply integrated as Databricks Vector Search.
questions.explanation: For a team that is building a RAG application on Databricks and wants a 'push-button' solution for their vector database, Databricks Vector Search is the clear choice. It is a fully managed and serverless offering, which means that the team doesn't have to worry about the operational overhead of setting up, managing, and scaling the database. It is also deeply integrated with the rest of the Databricks platform, which simplifies the overall architecture and makes it easier to build a robust and secure application.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that might have a 'yes' or 'no' answer. They want to ensure that for these types of questions, the LLM responds with only 'yes' or 'no'. Which of the following is the most reliable way to achieve this?
answers: Fine-tuning the LLM on a large dataset of yes/no questions.
Using a LangChain Output Parser that is designed to parse the LLM's response and to force it into a boolean (true/false) output.
Adding the instruction 'Answer with only yes or no' to the prompt.
Post-processing the LLM's output to check if it contains the word 'yes' or 'no'.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a very heavyweight solution for a simple formatting requirement.

Correct: A boolean output parser is the most reliable way to ensure that the final output is either 'yes' or 'no'. It can interpret a wide variety of the LLM's natural language responses (e.g., 'yes, that is correct', 'it appears so') and can normalize them to a simple boolean value.
Correct: This is a good first step and is often effective. However, for maximum reliability, it should be combined with an output parser.
Incorrect: This would be very brittle, as the LLM might respond in a way that doesn't use these exact words (e.g., 'that's affirmative').
questions.explanation: Getting a reliable boolean output from an LLM is a common requirement. The two best ways to achieve this in a LangChain application are to use an explicit instruction in the prompt and to use a boolean output parser. The prompt instruction tells the LLM what you want, and the output parser ensures that you get what you want, even if the LLM doesn't follow the instructions perfectly. The output parser can handle a variety of natural language responses and can convert them into a clean, reliable boolean value, which is exactly what you need for the downstream logic of your application.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of text documents that they need to chunk for a RAG application. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO of the main goals of the chunking process?
answers: To create chunks that are as large as possible.
To create chunks that are semantically coherent, meaning that they contain a complete idea or thought.
To create chunks that are small enough to fit within the context window of the embedding model and the LLM.
To create as many chunks as possible from each document.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Chunks that are too large can exceed the LLM's context window.
Correct: The goal of chunking is to create small, self-contained units of meaning that can be effectively embedded and retrieved.
Correct: This is a hard constraint of the chunking process. The chunks must be small enough to be processed by the downstream models.
Incorrect: The goal is to create high-quality chunks, not just a large number of them.
questions.explanation: The chunking process is a critical step in building a RAG application, and it has two main, sometimes competing, goals. The first goal is to create chunks that are semantically coherent. This means that you want each chunk to represent a complete thought or idea. This is important for both the embedding process (as it leads to more meaningful vectors) and for the generation process (as it provides the LLM with a clear and understandable piece of context). The second goal is to create chunks that are small enough to be handled by the embedding model and the LLM. Every model has a maximum context window, and your chunks must be smaller than that. A good chunking strategy is one that finds the right balance between these two goals.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to use an LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate the quality of its responses. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO key metrics that an LLM-as-a-judge can be used to evaluate?
answers: The latency of the RAG application's responses.
The faithfulness of the generated answer to the retrieved context.
The number of tokens in the generated answer.
The relevance of the generated answer to the user's question.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Latency is a performance metric that is measured with a stopwatch, not by an LLM judge.
Correct: You can provide the judge LLM with the generated answer and the retrieved context and ask it to determine if the answer is factually supported by the context.
Incorrect: This is a simple count and does not require an LLM judge.
Correct: You can provide the judge LLM with the user's question and the generated answer and ask it to score how well the answer addresses the question.
questions.explanation: LLM-as-a-judge is a powerful technique for evaluating the quality of a RAG application's output. Two of the most common and important metrics that it can be used to assess are faithfulness and answer relevancy. For faithfulness, the judge LLM is asked to act as a fact-checker, comparing the generated answer to the source documents to ensure that it is not hallucinating. For answer relevancy, the judge LLM is asked to act as a proxy for the user, determining how well the generated answer actually addresses the user's query. These two metrics together provide a strong signal of the overall quality of the RAG application.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by its finance department. The application will have access to sensitive financial data. Which TWO of the following Databricks features are most critical for ensuring the security and governance of this application?
answers: Databricks Repos for versioning the application's code.
Unity Catalog for defining fine-grained access control on the financial data.
The AI Playground for interactively testing the application.
Databricks Secrets for securely storing the credentials needed to access the financial data sources.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While code versioning is a good practice, it is not as critical for security and governance as Unity Catalog and Secrets.
Correct: Unity Catalog is the central tool for data governance on Databricks and is essential for ensuring that only authorized users can access the sensitive financial data.
Incorrect: The AI Playground is a development tool and does not provide production-level security and governance.
Correct: Databricks Secrets is the secure way to store and manage the credentials for any external data sources, which is a critical part of the overall security of the application.
questions.explanation: For an application that deals with sensitive data, security and governance are the top priorities. On Databricks, the two most critical features for achieving this are Unity Catalog and Databricks Secrets. Unity Catalog provides the comprehensive governance layer that allows you to define and enforce who can access what data. This is the cornerstone of the application's security. Databricks Secrets provides the secure mechanism for storing the credentials that the application needs to access the data. By using these two features together, you can build a RAG application that is both powerful and secure.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and wants to implement a 'query rewriting' step to improve retrieval quality. Which TWO of the following are valid examples of query rewriting?
answers: The user asks a vague question like 'tell me about our new product', and the LLM rewrites it into a series of more specific questions, such as 'What are the key features of the new product?', 'What is the price of the new product?', and 'What is the release date of the new product?'.
The user asks a question, and the LLM rewrites it to be more grammatically correct.
The user asks a question in a natural, conversational language, and the LLM rewrites it to include the specific technical terms that are used in the source documents.
The user asks a question, and the LLM rewrites it to be shorter and more concise.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a classic example of query expansion, which is a form of query rewriting. It can significantly improve retrieval by searching for the answers to several related questions at once.
Incorrect: While this might be a minor side effect, the main goal of query rewriting is to improve the semantic match with the documents, not just to fix grammar.
Correct: This is another key type of query rewriting. It helps to bridge the 'vocabulary gap' between the user and the documents.
Incorrect: Query rewriting often makes the query longer and more detailed, not shorter.
questions.explanation: Query rewriting is a powerful technique for improving the performance of a RAG system's retriever. The goal is to transform the user's initial query into a new query (or set of queries) that is more likely to retrieve the relevant documents. The two main ways to do this are query expansion and vocabulary mapping. In query expansion, the LLM generates a set of related, more specific questions to help find all the relevant information. In vocabulary mapping, the LLM 'translates' the user's natural language into the specific terminology used in the knowledge base. Both of these techniques can lead to a significant improvement in retrieval quality.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that are stored in a Delta table. They want to create a vector index that is optimized for fast query performance, even if it means that the index is not updated in real-time. Which type of Databricks Vector Search index is best suited for this requirement?
answers: A DELTA_SYNC index.
A DIRECT index.
A self-managed FAISS index.
A real-time index.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A DELTA_SYNC index is optimized for keeping the index in sync with the source table, not necessarily for the absolute fastest query performance.

Correct: A DIRECT index provides the lowest latency for queries because it reads the vectors directly from the source table. It is a good choice when the source table does not change frequently and when query performance is the top priority.
Incorrect: While FAISS is performant, a DIRECT index in Databricks Vector Search is a more integrated and managed solution for this specific use case.
Incorrect: This is a general term, not a specific type of Databricks Vector Search index.
questions.explanation: Databricks Vector Search offers two main types of indexes: DELTA_SYNC and DIRECT. A DELTA_SYNC index is designed to automatically stay in sync with a source Delta table, which is great for data that changes frequently. A DIRECT index, on the other hand, is designed for maximum query performance. It reads the vectors and data directly from the source table at query time, which can provide lower latency than a DELTA_SYNC index. For a use case where the data is relatively static and the top priority is fast queries, a DIRECT index is the best choice.

questions.question: A company is preparing to deploy a new RAG application and is conducting a final round of evaluations. They want to ensure that the application does not provide harmful or biased answers. Which TWO of the following evaluation techniques are most relevant for this?
answers: Measuring the ROUGE score of the generated answers against a set of golden answers.
Conducting a 'red teaming' exercise where testers intentionally try to provoke the model into generating undesirable content.
Using a specialized evaluation dataset that is designed to test for bias across different demographic groups.
Measuring the latency of the responses.
feedbacks: Incorrect: ROUGE measures n-gram overlap and is not a good metric for detecting bias or harmfulness.
Correct: Red teaming is the most effective way to proactively identify and mitigate the risks of a model producing harmful or biased content.

Correct: There are a number of open-source and commercial datasets that are specifically designed to test for social and demographic biases in LLMs. Using these datasets is a key part of a responsible AI evaluation plan.
Incorrect: Latency is a performance metric and has no bearing on the safety or fairness of the responses.
questions.explanation: Ensuring the safety and fairness of a generative AI application is a critical part of the pre-deployment process. The two most important evaluation techniques for this are red teaming and using bias evaluation datasets. Red teaming is a proactive, adversarial testing process where you try to make the model fail in harmful ways. This is the best way to find the 'unknown unknowns' in your model's safety profile. Using a specialized bias evaluation dataset is a more systematic way to test for known types of social and demographic biases. A responsible AI development process should include both of these techniques.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application to Databricks Model Serving. The application is becoming very popular, and they are concerned about the rising costs of the LLM inference. Which TWO of the following are effective strategies to reduce the cost of the application without significantly degrading the user experience?
answers: Implementing a caching layer to store and reuse the answers to frequently asked questions.
Switching to a larger and more powerful LLM.
Using a smaller, less expensive LLM for simpler queries, and only using the large LLM for more complex queries.
Increasing the number of documents retrieved for each query to provide more context.
feedbacks: Correct: Caching is one of the most effective ways to reduce the number of calls to the LLM, which can lead to significant cost savings.
Incorrect: A larger LLM would almost certainly be more expensive.
Correct: This 'model routing' approach is a powerful cost optimization technique. It ensures that you are only using the expensive model when it is truly needed.
Incorrect: This would increase the size of the prompt and therefore the cost of each query.
questions.explanation: Managing the cost of a popular RAG application is a common challenge. The two most effective strategies for this are caching and model routing. Caching is a simple but powerful technique that can eliminate a large number of redundant calls to the LLM by reusing the answers to common questions. Model routing is a more advanced technique where you use a 'router' model to classify the user's query and then send it to the most appropriate LLM. Simple queries can be handled by a small, fast, and cheap model, while only the most complex queries are sent to the large, expensive model. The combination of these two techniques can lead to a dramatic reduction in the overall cost of the application.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and wants to give the LLM access to a set of pre-defined functions that it can call. For example, they want the LLM to be able to call a function to look up the current weather. This capability is known as:
answers: Function calling or tool use.
Prompt engineering.
Fine-tuning.
Retrieval-augmented generation.
feedbacks: Correct: 'Function calling' (the term used by OpenAI) and 'tool use' (the more general term, used by LangChain and others) refer to the ability of an LLM to call external functions or tools.
Incorrect: While prompting is used to enable function calling, the capability itself is more than just prompting.
Incorrect: Fine-tuning is a process of training the model and is not the same as giving it the ability to call functions at inference time.

Incorrect: RAG is about retrieving documents to provide context to the LLM. Function calling is about giving the LLM the ability to take actions. While they can be used together in an agent, they are distinct concepts.
questions.explanation: The ability for an LLM to call external functions or tools is a major advance in generative AI and is a key enabler for building powerful agents and applications. This capability, often referred to as 'function calling' or 'tool use', allows the LLM to go beyond simply generating text and to interact with the outside world. By giving the LLM access to a set of tools, you can create applications that can answer questions about real-time data, interact with other software systems, and perform a wide variety of tasks.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by its legal team to search through a large number of sensitive legal documents. Which TWO of the following Databricks features are essential for building a secure and compliant application for this use case?
answers: The AI Playground.
Unity Catalog for providing fine-grained access control and end-to-end data lineage.
Databricks Model Serving for deploying the application with high availability.
Lakehouse Federation to connect to an external, less secure database.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The AI Playground is for experimentation and is not a security or compliance tool.

Correct: For a legal use case, audibility and access control are paramount. Unity Catalog provides the necessary features to ensure that only authorized users can access the documents and that there is a complete audit trail of how the data is used.
Incorrect: While high availability is important, it is not as critical for security and compliance as the governance features.
Incorrect: For a sensitive use case, you would want to keep the data within the secure environment of the lakehouse, not connect to less secure external systems.
questions.explanation: For a sensitive use case like legal discovery, the security and governance of the application are the most important considerations. On Databricks, Unity Catalog is the cornerstone of this. It provides two essential capabilities for a legal application: fine-grained access control and data lineage. Fine-grained access control ensures that the strict 'need-to-know' policies of a legal team can be enforced at the data layer. Data lineage provides a complete, auditable trail of how the data has been used, which is often a critical requirement for legal and compliance purposes.

questions.question: A developer is working with a LangChain chain and wants to pass the output of one component to two other components in parallel. For example, they want to pass a user's query to both a web search tool and a document retrieval tool at the same time. Which LangChain component is designed for this kind of parallel execution?
answers: The `|` (pipe) operator.
The `RunnableParallel` class (which can also be represented as a dictionary).
A for loop in Python.
The `AgentExecutor` class.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The pipe operator is for creating sequential chains, where the output of one component is the input to the next.

Correct: `RunnableParallel` is the LangChain component that allows you to run multiple `Runnable` objects in parallel. You can define a dictionary where each value is a `Runnable`, and LangChain will execute them all concurrently.

Incorrect: While you could write a for loop to call multiple components, `RunnableParallel` is the idiomatic and more powerful way to handle parallel execution within the LangChain Expression Language.
Incorrect: While an agent can use multiple tools, `RunnableParallel` is the specific component for explicit parallel execution of `Runnable` objects.
questions.explanation: LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) provides a powerful and flexible way to compose different components. For sequential execution, you use the pipe (`|`) operator. For parallel execution, you use the `RunnableParallel` class. A `RunnableParallel` can be defined as a dictionary where each key-value pair represents a parallel branch of execution. LangChain will run all of these branches concurrently and will return a dictionary with the results. This is a very powerful feature for building complex chains that need to perform multiple tasks at the same time.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that contain a mix of plain text and tables. They want to create a single text representation for each document that includes the information from the tables. Which of the following is the most effective way to do this?
answers: Ignoring the tables and just using the plain text.

Converting the tables to a human-readable, text-based format, such as Markdown or a simple key-value representation, and then inserting this text into the document where the table originally appeared.
Taking a screenshot of each table and using an OCR tool to extract the text.
Creating a separate document for each table.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would lose the valuable information in the tables.

Correct: This is the most effective approach. By converting the table to a text format that preserves its structure and meaning, you can create a single, coherent text document that can be effectively used by the RAG system.
Incorrect: This is a very roundabout and likely error-prone way to handle digitally native tables.
Incorrect: This would separate the tables from their context in the rest of the document.
questions.explanation: When you have documents with a mix of text and tables, the best approach for a RAG system is to create a single, unified text representation that includes the information from the tables. To do this, you first need to parse the tables and convert them into a text-based format that preserves their structure. Markdown tables are a great choice for this, as they are both human-readable and machine-readable. You can then insert this Markdown representation of the table back into the main text of the document. This creates a single, coherent text document that contains all the information from the original file, which can then be effectively chunked and embedded.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions about a company's internal organizational chart. The org chart is stored in a graph database. Which of the following is the most effective way for the RAG application to use this data?
answers: Exporting the graph database to a set of text documents and using a standard RAG approach.
Creating a LangChain agent that has a 'tool' for querying the graph database (e.g., with a Cypher or GraphQL query).
Fine-tuning the LLM on a large number of questions and answers about the org chart.
Representing the org chart as a single, very large JSON object and passing it in the prompt to the LLM.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would lose the valuable graph structure of the data.
Correct: This is the most powerful and flexible approach. The agent can use the LLM's reasoning capabilities to construct a query for the graph database based on the user's question.
Incorrect: While this could help, it would be a static solution and would not be able to answer questions about a constantly changing org chart. An agent-based approach is much more flexible.
Incorrect: This would likely exceed the LLM's context window and would not be an efficient way to query the data.
questions.explanation: When you have data that is stored in a structured format like a graph database, the best way to use it in a RAG application is to give the LLM the ability to query that data directly. The 'agent-with-tools' paradigm is perfect for this. You would create a tool that knows how to connect to the graph database and execute a query, and you would give this tool to a LangChain agent. The agent could then take a user's question, like 'Who is John Smith's manager?', and use the LLM to convert that question into a formal query for the graph database. This is a much more powerful and flexible approach than trying to flatten the graph into text.

questions.question: A team has deployed a RAG application and has set up a monitoring system that tracks the user feedback. They notice that the percentage of 'thumbs down' ratings has been slowly increasing over the past month. This is a classic example of what kind of problem in a production machine learning system?
answers: A software bug.
Concept drift or data drift.
A hardware failure.
A security breach.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While it could be a bug, a slow, gradual decline in performance is more likely to be drift.

Correct: This is the most likely cause. Drift occurs when the statistical properties of the data change over time. In a RAG application, this could mean that users are starting to ask about new topics, or that the content of the knowledge base is becoming outdated. This leads to a gradual degradation in the application's performance.
Incorrect: A hardware failure would likely cause a sudden and catastrophic failure, not a slow decline in performance.
Incorrect: While a security breach is a serious issue, it would not typically manifest as a slow decline in the quality of the application's responses.
questions.explanation: A slow, gradual decline in the performance of a machine learning system is the classic sign of model drift or data drift. In the context of a RAG application, this can happen for a number of reasons. The topics that users are interested in can change over time (concept drift), or the information in the knowledge base can become stale and out-of-date (data drift). This is why continuous monitoring and evaluation are so important for production AI systems. By tracking the performance of the application over time, the team can detect this drift and can take action to retrain their models or to update their data.

questions.question: A data engineer is preparing a dataset of scientific papers for a RAG application. The papers are in PDF format and contain a lot of complex mathematical formulas. Which TWO of the following are the most effective ways to handle these formulas?
answers: Ignoring the formulas and only extracting the text.
Converting the formulas to a high-resolution image and using an image embedding model.
Using a document parsing tool that can recognize the formulas and can convert them to a structured, text-based format, such as LaTeX.
Representing each formula with a placeholder token, such as '[FORMULA]'.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The formulas often contain the most important information in a scientific paper.
Incorrect: While this is a possible approach, it is very complex and is not the most effective way to handle the structured information in the formulas.

Correct: The best approach is to use a specialized parsing tool that can understand the structure of the formulas and can convert them to a format like LaTeX. The LaTeX string can then be included in the text that is embedded, providing a perfect, machine-readable representation of the formula.
Incorrect: This would lose all the information contained in the formula.
questions.explanation: Handling mathematical formulas is a challenging but important task for any RAG system that works with scientific documents. The key is to use a document parsing tool that is specifically designed to handle this type of content. A good scientific document parser will be able to recognize the mathematical formulas within a PDF and can convert them to a structured, text-based format like LaTeX. The LaTeX representation of the formula can then be included in the text that is chunked and embedded. This provides a perfect, unambiguous representation of the formula that can be understood by the LLM, which has been trained on a large amount of scientific text that includes LaTeX.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to track its business impact. The application is a customer support chatbot, and its goal is to reduce the number of support tickets that need to be handled by a human agent. Which of the following is the most relevant metric for evaluating the business impact of this application?
answers: The average ROUGE score of the chatbot's answers.
The ticket deflection rate, which is the percentage of customer queries that are successfully resolved by the chatbot without escalating to a human agent.
The average number of turns in a conversation with the chatbot.
The number of 'thumbs up' ratings that the chatbot receives.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this is a measure of quality, it is not a direct measure of the business impact.

Correct: This is a direct measure of the chatbot's success in achieving its primary business goal. A high ticket deflection rate means that the chatbot is saving the company money and freeing up the human agents to work on more complex issues.
Incorrect: This is an engagement metric, but it doesn't necessarily correlate with the business impact.
Incorrect: While user satisfaction is important, the ticket deflection rate is a more direct and quantitative measure of the business value.
questions.explanation: When evaluating the success of a RAG application, it's important to go beyond technical metrics and to measure its impact on the business. For a customer support chatbot, the most important business metric is the ticket deflection rate. This metric directly measures how effective the chatbot is at its core task: resolving customer issues without the need for human intervention. By tracking the ticket deflection rate, the company can get a clear and quantitative understanding of the return on investment (ROI) of their RAG application.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and has decided to use a fine-tuned LLM to improve its performance. Which TWO of the following are the most likely reasons why they would choose to fine-tune the LLM?
answers: To give the LLM access to real-time information.
To teach the LLM the specific writing style and tone of the company's brand.
To improve the LLM's understanding of the company's domain-specific jargon and concepts.
To reduce the latency of the LLM's responses.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Fine-tuning is on a static dataset and does not provide access to real-time data. RAG is the technique for that.
Correct: Fine-tuning is very effective at adapting the style and tone of an LLM.
Correct: Fine-tuning on a corpus of company documents can significantly improve the LLM's ability to understand and to use the specific language of that domain.
Incorrect: Fine-tuning can sometimes increase latency, and it is not the primary reason for doing it.
questions.explanation: While RAG is a powerful technique for providing an LLM with factual knowledge, fine-tuning is the best way to adapt its fundamental behavior and knowledge base. The two most common and compelling reasons to fine-tune an LLM for a RAG application are to teach it a specific style and to improve its understanding of a specific domain. By fine-tuning on a dataset of examples that reflect the desired brand voice, you can make the LLM's responses much more consistent and on-brand. By fine-tuning on a large corpus of domain-specific documents, you can help the model to internalize the concepts and jargon of that domain, which can lead to a significant improvement in the quality and relevance of its responses.

questions.question: A data engineer is building the data pipeline for a RAG application. They are using Delta Live Tables to ingest and to transform the source documents. Which TWO of the following are key benefits of using Delta Live Tables for this purpose?
answers: It provides a user interface for non-technical users to build data pipelines.
It automatically manages the dependencies between the steps in the pipeline and can execute them in the correct order.
It has built-in support for data quality checks, which can be used to ensure the reliability of the data that is fed into the RAG system.
It is the only way to create Delta tables on Databricks.
feedbacks: Incorrect: DLT is a code-first, declarative framework for data engineers.
Correct: A key feature of DLT is that it automatically infers the data lineage and manages the execution of the pipeline, which simplifies development and improves reliability.
Correct: DLT has powerful, built-in features for defining and enforcing data quality constraints, which is essential for building a trustworthy RAG application.
Incorrect: You can create Delta tables with standard Spark SQL or DataFrame APIs.
questions.explanation: Delta Live Tables is a powerful framework for building reliable and maintainable data pipelines on Databricks, and it is an excellent choice for the data preparation stage of a RAG application. Two of its key benefits are its automatic dependency management and its built-in data quality features. DLT automatically understands the lineage of your data and will execute the steps of your pipeline in the correct order, which simplifies the development process. It also has a rich set of features for defining and enforcing data quality rules, which allows you to ensure that the data you are feeding into your RAG system is clean, correct, and reliable.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application that uses a pay-per-token foundation model. They want to track the costs of the application. Which TWO of the following Databricks features would be most useful for this?
answers: Databricks Model Serving inference tables, which log the number of input and output tokens for each request.
The system tables in Unity Catalog, which can provide detailed usage and cost information for various Databricks services.
The AI Playground.
The Databricks cluster UI.
feedbacks: Correct: The inference tables can be configured to log the token counts for each request, which provides the raw data needed to calculate the cost.

Correct: Databricks is increasingly making detailed usage and audit information available through system tables. These can be queried to get a comprehensive view of costs, including those related to model serving.
Incorrect: The AI Playground is for interactive experimentation and does not provide cost tracking information.
Incorrect: The cluster UI shows the cost of the cluster's compute, but it does not provide a detailed breakdown of the costs associated with a specific model serving endpoint.
questions.explanation: Tracking the cost of a pay-per-token RAG application is crucial for managing its budget. On Databricks, the two best ways to get this information are from the inference tables and the system tables.
