Correct: You could also use a recursive character text splitter and configure it to only use the newline character as a separator. This would have the same effect as a simple split but might be more convenient if you are using a standardized chunking pipeline.
questions.explanation: When you are working with data that has a very clear, line-based structure, the best chunking strategy is one that respects that structure. The most direct way to do this is to simply split the text by the newline character. This will ensure that each line of the original document becomes a separate chunk. You can also achieve the same result with a recursive character text splitter, by configuring it to use the newline character as its primary separator. Both of these approaches will do a much better job of preserving the structure of the data than a more generic strategy like fixed-size or semantic chunking.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to track the user journey through the application. For example, they want to see what follow-up questions users are asking after they get an initial answer. Which of the following is the best way to get this information?
answers: Analyzing the inference tables and looking for patterns in the sequence of requests from a single user or session.
Conducting a usability test where you specifically ask users to perform a multi-step task.
Looking at the data lineage in Unity Catalog.
Asking the LLM to predict what the user's next question will be.
feedbacks: Correct: If the inference tables include a user or session ID, you can use this to reconstruct the sequence of queries from a single user, which can provide a lot of insight into their journey.
Correct: A targeted usability test is an excellent way to get a deep, qualitative understanding of the user journey and to identify any points of friction or confusion.
Incorrect: Data lineage shows how the data flows through the backend systems, not how the user flows through the application.
Incorrect: This would be a speculative and an unreliable way to understand the actual user journey.
questions.explanation: Understanding the user journey is key to improving the user experience of a RAG application. The two best ways to do this are to analyze the usage data and to conduct targeted user research. By analyzing the sequence of queries from a single user or session in your inference tables, you can get a quantitative understanding of the common user journeys. To get a deeper, more qualitative understanding, you can conduct a usability test where you give users a specific goal and then watch them as they try to achieve it with your application. The combination of these two methods will give you a rich and actionable understanding of the user journey.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and has chosen to fine-tune the LLM to improve its performance on their specific domain. Which TWO of the following are the most important prerequisites for a successful fine-tuning effort?
answers: A very large and powerful GPU.
A high-quality dataset of examples that are representative of the task that you want the model to perform.
A clear set of evaluation metrics and a robust evaluation pipeline to measure the performance of the fine-tuned model.
A team of PhD-level research scientists.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While a GPU is necessary for fine-tuning, the size and power are not the most important prerequisite. The quality of the data is more important.
Correct: The quality and the relevance of the fine-tuning data is the single most important factor in the success of a fine-tuning project. Garbage in, garbage out.
Correct: You can't improve what you can't measure. A solid evaluation plan is essential for knowing if your fine-tuning efforts are actually making the model better.
Incorrect: While expertise is helpful, you don't need a team of research scientists to successfully fine-tune an LLM, especially with the tools and platforms that are available today.
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning an LLM can be a powerful technique, but it requires a disciplined approach. The two most important prerequisites for success are a high-quality dataset and a robust evaluation plan. The dataset is the raw material that you will use to teach the model, and its quality will directly determine the quality of the final, fine-tuned model. The evaluation plan is how you will measure your progress and how you will know if you have succeeded. Without a good dataset and a good evaluation plan, a fine-tuning project is very likely to fail.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that contain a mix of natural language text and source code snippets. Which of the following is the most effective chunking strategy for this data?
answers: Treating the entire document as a single chunk.
Using a text splitter that is aware of the syntax of the programming language and can keep the code snippets together as a single, coherent chunk.
Stripping out all the code snippets and only using the natural language text.
Using a recursive character text splitter with separators that are designed to handle both prose (e.g., splitting by paragraphs and sentences) and code (e.g., splitting by functions or classes).
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would likely exceed the context window and would not be good for retrieval.

Correct: The best approach is to use a chunking strategy that can differentiate between the natural language text and the code. There are specialized text splitters that can parse the code and can ensure that a complete function or a class is kept together in a single chunk.
Incorrect: The code snippets are a critical part of the information in the document.

Correct: A well-configured recursive character text splitter can be a very effective way to handle documents with a mix of text and code. You can provide a set of separators that are appropriate for both types of content.
questions.explanation: When you have documents that contain both natural language and source code, you need a chunking strategy that can handle both. The best approach is to use a splitter that is 'language-aware' and can identify the boundaries of the code blocks. This ensures that a complete function or a code snippet is not broken up across multiple chunks. A well-configured recursive character text splitter can also be a very good solution. By providing it with a set of separators that are appropriate for both the prose and the code, you can create a chunking strategy that respects the structure of both types of content.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to set up a dashboard to monitor its operational health. Which TWO of the following are the most important metrics to include on this dashboard?
answers: The number of 'thumbs up' ratings from users.
The error rate of the model serving endpoint.
The latency of the model serving endpoint.
The ROUGE score of the generated responses.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this is a good measure of user satisfaction, it is not a direct measure of the operational health of the system.
Correct: The error rate is a critical metric for operational health. A high error rate indicates that there is a problem with the service that needs to be investigated immediately.
Correct: Latency is another critical operational metric. A spike in latency can indicate a problem with the system and can lead to a poor user experience.
Incorrect: This is a quality metric, not an operational health metric.
questions.explanation: An operational health dashboard is designed to give you an at-a-glance view of the status of your production systems. For a RAG application that is deployed on Databricks Model Serving, the two most important operational metrics to track are the error rate and the latency of the serving endpoint. The error rate tells you if the service is available and is processing requests correctly. The latency tells you if the service is performing well. By monitoring these two metrics and by setting up alerts on them, you can ensure that you are quickly notified of any operational issues with your application.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used in a regulated industry. They have a strict requirement for audibility, and they need to be able to demonstrate to an auditor exactly how any given answer was generated. Which TWO Databricks features are most critical for meeting this requirement?
answers: The AI Playground.
Unity Catalog's data lineage capabilities, which can show the full history of the data used in the RAG application.
MLflow's integration with LangChain, which allows the entire RAG chain to be logged as a versioned model, providing a clear record of the application's logic.
The ability to use open-source models.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The AI Playground is for interactive development and does not provide an audit trail.

Correct: Data lineage is a key feature for audibility. Unity Catalog can provide a complete, end-to-end lineage graph that shows exactly where the data came from and how it was transformed, which is essential for any audit.

Correct: By logging the RAG chain as a versioned model in MLflow, you create a clear and immutable record of the exact logic that was used to generate the answers. This is another critical component of a robust audit trail.
Incorrect: The choice of model is not as important for audibility as the ability to track the data and the application logic.
questions.explanation: For a regulated industry where audibility is a key requirement, you need to be able to provide a complete and transparent record of how your RAG application works. On Databricks, the two most critical features for this are Unity Catalog's data lineage and MLflow's model versioning. Data lineage from Unity Catalog provides the audit trail for the data, showing exactly what information was used by the application. MLflow's ability to log and to version the entire RAG chain provides the audit trail for the application's logic. By combining these two, you can provide an auditor with a comprehensive, end-to-end explanation of how any given answer was generated.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain application and wants to create a chain that first retrieves some documents and then passes those documents to a prompt. Which of the following is the most idiomatic way to do this in LCEL?
answers: `prompt.format(context=retriever.get_relevant_documents(query))`
`{'context': retriever, 'question': RunnablePassthrough()} | prompt`
`retriever | prompt`
`RunnableParallel(retriever=retriever, question=RunnablePassthrough()) | prompt`
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a standard Python function call and does not create a composable LCEL chain.

Correct: This is the standard and most idiomatic LCEL pattern for a RAG chain. It creates a dictionary where the 'context' is populated by the retriever and the 'question' is passed through from the initial input. This dictionary is then passed to the prompt.
Incorrect: This would pass the list of documents directly to the prompt, but the prompt also needs the original question. The pattern in the correct answer is the way to pass both.

Correct: This is another, more explicit way to write the exact same logic as the dictionary-based syntax. `RunnableParallel` can be initialized with a dictionary, and it will execute the runnables in parallel. For RAG, this is the standard pattern.
questions.explanation: The 'hello world' of LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) is the simple RAG chain. The standard pattern for this is to use a `RunnableParallel` (which can be expressed as a dictionary) to run the retriever and to pass through the original question in parallel. This creates a dictionary with the keys `context` and `question`. This dictionary is then piped to the prompt template, which has input variables for `context` and `question`. This elegant and composable pattern is the foundation for building almost all RAG applications in LangChain.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that have a mix of very long and very short sentences. They are concerned that a sentence-based chunking strategy will create chunks of very different sizes, which might not be optimal. Which of the following chunking strategies would be a better choice?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Semantic chunking.
Combining all the documents into one and then splitting it into N equal parts.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Fixed-size chunking is even more likely to create suboptimal chunks, as it will cut sentences in the middle.

Correct: A recursive character text splitter is a great choice for this scenario. It can be configured to split by sentences first, but then to further split or to group the sentences to create chunks that are of a more uniform size.

Correct: Semantic chunking is another excellent choice. It is not based on sentence boundaries at all, but rather on the semantic meaning of the text. It will naturally create chunks that are semantically coherent, regardless of the length of the sentences.
Incorrect: This would be a very poor chunking strategy.
questions.explanation: When you have text with a lot of variation in sentence length, a simple sentence-based chunking strategy can be problematic. The two best alternatives are to use a recursive character text splitter or to use semantic chunking. A recursive splitter can be configured to create chunks that are within a certain size range, which can help to normalize the chunk length. Semantic chunking is an even more advanced approach that ignores sentence boundaries altogether and instead creates chunks based on the meaning of the text. Both of these methods will produce a much more uniform and a much higher-quality set of chunks than a simple sentence-based splitter.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to start a continuous improvement process. Which TWO of the following are the most important inputs to this process?
answers: The version of the Python libraries used in the application.
Feedback from the users of the application, for example, from a 'thumbs up' / 'thumbs down' rating system.
Analysis of the queries that the application is failing on, or for which it is providing low-quality answers.
The number of hours that the development team has worked on the application.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a technical detail and is not a primary input to the continuous improvement process.
Correct: User feedback is one of the most valuable sources of information for understanding what is working and what is not.
Correct: By analyzing the failures of the application, the team can identify the key areas for improvement. This is a classic data-driven approach to continuous improvement.
Incorrect: This is a measure of effort, not of quality or of user satisfaction.
questions.explanation: A continuous improvement process for a RAG application is all about using data to make the application better over time. The two most important sources of this data are the users and the application's own failures. User feedback provides a direct signal of what the users think about the application. An analysis of the application's failures (which can be identified from the user feedback or from an automated evaluation process) provides a more technical signal of where the system is weak. By combining these two inputs, the team can create a data-driven roadmap for continuously improving their application.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application that will be used by its entire global workforce. They need to ensure that the application is highly available and can tolerate the failure of an entire cloud region. Which TWO of the following are the most important architectural components for achieving this?
answers: Deploying the application to a single, very large cluster in a single region.
Deploying the application to multiple availability zones within a single region.
Deploying the application to multiple, geographically distributed cloud regions.
Using a global load balancer that can detect the failure of a region and can automatically reroute traffic to a healthy region.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be a single point of failure and would not be highly available.
Incorrect: While this provides protection against the failure of a single data center, it does not protect against the failure of an entire region.
Correct: A multi-region deployment is the standard architecture for achieving high availability and disaster recovery.
Correct: A global load balancer is the key component that makes a multi-region deployment work. It provides the automated failover capability that is needed for high availability.
questions.explanation: For a mission-critical, global application, high availability is a key requirement. The standard and most effective architecture for this is a multi-region deployment with a global load balancer. By deploying the application to two or more geographically distributed cloud regions, you can ensure that it can survive the complete failure of a single region. The global load balancer is the 'brains' of this architecture. It monitors the health of the application in each region and will automatically reroute all traffic to a healthy region if it detects a failure. This provides a seamless and automated failover experience for the users.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that have a single, definitive, factual answer (e.g., 'What is the capital of France?'). The knowledge base for the application is a set of encyclopedia articles. Which of the following RAG architectures would be most appropriate?
answers: A simple RAG chain that retrieves the most relevant article and passes it to the LLM to extract the answer.
An agent-based architecture with multiple tools.
A RAG system that uses a fine-tuned LLM.
A system that does not use retrieval and just relies on the LLM's pre-trained knowledge.
feedbacks: Correct: For simple, factual question-answering, a simple RAG chain is often the most effective and efficient architecture.
Incorrect: An agent is overkill for this kind of simple, factual question-answering.
Incorrect: While fine-tuning could potentially improve performance, it is not necessary for this kind of straightforward task. A standard foundation model in a RAG pipeline should be sufficient.

Incorrect: While the LLM might know the answer to this specific question, for a general-purpose encyclopedia application, a RAG approach is much more reliable, as it can ground the answer in a specific source document.
questions.explanation: For simple, factual question-answering, a simple RAG chain is the most appropriate and efficient architecture. The process is straightforward: the user's question is used to retrieve the most relevant document (or documents) from the knowledge base, and then the LLM is used to read the retrieved document and to extract the answer. There is no need for the complexity of a multi-tool agent or for the expense of a fine-tuned model. A simple, well-constructed RAG chain can be very effective for this kind of task.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents and wants to use an embedding model that is provided as a foundation model API on Databricks. Which of the following is the best way to call this API on a large number of documents in a Spark DataFrame?
answers: Using a standard Python UDF to call the API for each row of the DataFrame.
Using a Pandas UDF to call the API with batches of documents.
Collecting all the documents to the driver node and then calling the API from a single thread.
Using the MLflow API to call the embedding model.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A row-at-a-time UDF would be very inefficient and would not take advantage of the batching capabilities of the API.

Correct: The foundation model APIs are optimized for batch processing. A Pandas UDF is the most efficient way to call these APIs from Spark, as it allows you to send a batch of documents in a single API call, which significantly reduces the overhead.
Incorrect: This would not be scalable and would likely cause the driver to run out of memory.
Incorrect: The MLflow API is for tracking and managing models, not for calling them for inference at scale.
questions.explanation: When you need to call a foundation model API for embedding on a large Spark DataFrame, the key to performance is batching. The APIs are designed to be much more efficient when you send them a batch of documents at once. The best way to do this from Spark is to use a Pandas UDF. A Pandas UDF allows you to work with batches of data (as Pandas DataFrames) within your Spark job. This means you can take a batch of documents, send them to the embedding API in a single call, and then return the results to Spark. This is a much more performant and scalable approach than a row-at-a-time UDF.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to evaluate its performance on a continuous basis. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO of the main benefits of setting up a continuous evaluation pipeline?
answers: It allows the company to eliminate the need for a development team.
It allows the team to quickly detect and to respond to any regressions in the application's performance.
It provides a data-driven way to measure the impact of any changes or improvements made to the application.
It guarantees that the application will always be 100% accurate.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A continuous evaluation pipeline is a tool for the development team, not a replacement for them.
Correct: By running the evaluation on a regular basis, the team can quickly catch any new bugs or performance issues that are introduced by changes to the code or the data.
Correct: When the team makes a change to the application, they can use the continuous evaluation pipeline to get a quantitative measure of whether that change actually improved the performance.
Incorrect: No evaluation pipeline can guarantee 100% accuracy.
questions.explanation: A continuous evaluation pipeline is a cornerstone of a mature MLOps for LLM practice. It has two main benefits. First, it acts as a safety net, allowing the team to quickly detect and to respond to any regressions in the application's performance. This is essential for maintaining a high level of quality in a production application. Second, it provides the data that the team needs to make informed decisions about how to improve the application. By providing a quantitative measure of the impact of any changes, the continuous evaluation pipeline enables a data-driven, iterative approach to development.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to ensure that it can be easily rolled back to a previous version if a problem is discovered in production. Which TWO of the following are the most important prerequisites for this?
answers: A detailed log of all the user queries to the application.
Using a version control system (like Git) for the application's code.
Using a model registry (like the MLflow Model Registry) to version the RAG chain and the other model assets.
Having a very fast development team.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While useful for debugging, this is not a prerequisite for being able to roll back the application.
Correct: To be able to roll back the code, you must have the previous versions of the code stored in a version control system.
Correct: To be able to roll back the AI components of the application, you must have the previous versions of those components stored and versioned in a model registry.
Incorrect: While a fast team is nice to have, the ability to roll back depends on having a good versioning and deployment process, not on the speed of the team.
questions.explanation: The ability to quickly and reliably roll back to a previous version is a key part of a robust deployment process. To be able to do this for a RAG application, you need to have a versioned copy of all the application's components. This means that the application's code should be stored in a version control system like Git, and the AI assets (like the RAG chain and the embedding model) should be stored and versioned in a model registry like MLflow. With these two things in place, you can easily redeploy a previous, known-good version of the application if you ever encounter a critical issue in production.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that require some mathematical calculation. For example, 'If a product costs $120 and is on sale for 25% off, what is the final price?' Which of the following is the best way to enable this capability?
answers: Fine-tuning the LLM on a large dataset of math problems.
Creating a LangChain agent that has access to a 'calculator' tool.
Asking the LLM to 'think step-by-step' and to show its work.
Representing all the numbers as words (e.g., 'one hundred and twenty') to make it easier for the LLM.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this can improve the LLM's math skills, it is not a reliable way to ensure accurate calculations. LLMs are notoriously bad at math.

Correct: The best and most reliable way to perform calculations in an LLM application is to give the agent a tool that can call a standard calculator or a Python interpreter. The LLM can then offload the calculation to this tool, which will always be accurate.
Incorrect: While this can sometimes help the LLM to reason about the problem better, it does not guarantee that the final calculation will be correct.
Incorrect: This would make it harder, not easier, for the LLM to perform the calculation.
questions.explanation: Large language models are masters of text, but they are not very good at performing precise mathematical calculations. The best and most reliable way to add math capabilities to a RAG application is to use the 'agent-with-tools' paradigm. You would create a simple tool that can perform calculations (e.g., by calling the Python interpreter) and you would give this tool to your agent. The agent's LLM can then be used to understand the user's question and to extract the necessary information to call the calculator tool. This approach combines the language understanding capabilities of the LLM with the mathematical precision of a traditional calculator, giving you the best of both worlds.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that are very long and cover multiple different topics. Which of the following is the most effective chunking strategy for this type of document?
answers: Using a very large chunk size to try to capture all the topics in a single chunk.
Using a text splitter that can split the document based on its logical structure (e.g., by chapters or sections).
Using a semantic chunking strategy that can identify the points in the document where the topic changes.
Using a fixed-size chunking strategy.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be effective for retrieval, as the meaning of the chunk would be very diluted.
Correct: If the document has a logical structure, using a chunking strategy that respects that structure is the best way to create coherent chunks that are focused on a single topic.
Correct: For a long document that covers multiple topics, semantic chunking can be a very effective way to break it up into a set of smaller, topically-focused chunks.
Incorrect: A fixed-size strategy would likely create chunks that contain a mix of different topics, which would not be good for retrieval.
questions.explanation: When you have long documents that cover multiple topics, the key to a good chunking strategy is to create chunks that are as topically focused as possible. The two best ways to do this are to use a structure-aware splitter or to use a semantic chunker. If the document has a clear hierarchical structure (like chapters and sections), you should use a splitter that can leverage that structure to create your chunks. If the document does not have a clear structure, a semantic chunker can be used to automatically identify the topic boundaries in the text. Both of these approaches will produce a set of high-quality, topically-focused chunks that are ideal for a RAG application.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and has set up a continuous evaluation pipeline that runs on a daily basis. MLflow, which can be used to log the metrics from each evaluation run as an experiment. The MLflow UI can then be used to visualize and to compare the runs.
A Databricks Dashboard, which can be configured to query the table where the evaluation results are logged and to display the metrics in a set of charts and graphs.
A plain text file where the results of each run are appended.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The web terminal is a command-line interface and is not a good tool for visualizing and tracking metrics.

Correct: MLflow is the perfect tool for this. You can treat each daily evaluation as an MLflow run and can log the key quality metrics to it. The MLflow UI then provides a powerful interface for tracking these metrics over time.

Correct: A Databricks Dashboard is another excellent option. It provides a flexible and customizable way to visualize the evaluation results and to create a high-level overview of the application's performance.
Incorrect: This would not be a good way to visualize or to analyze the results.
questions.explanation: Once you have a continuous evaluation pipeline, you need a good way to visualize and to track the results. On Databricks, the two best tools for this are MLflow and Databricks Dashboards. You can log the results of each evaluation run to MLflow, which gives you a detailed, experiment-tracking view of the performance over time. You can also log the results to a Delta table and then build a Databricks Dashboard on top of that table. This provides a more high-level, customizable view of the key metrics. Many teams will use a combination of both of these tools to get a complete picture of their application's performance.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to ensure that they are following MLOps best practices. Which TWO of the following are the most important MLOps practices for a RAG application?
answers: Managing the application's code and its dependencies in a version control system.
Automating the testing and the deployment of the application with a CI/CD pipeline.
Having a single developer who is responsible for the entire application, from development to deployment.
Manually deploying the application by copying the files to the production server.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a fundamental best practice for all software development, including MLOps. It's essential for reproducibility and for collaboration.

Correct: A CI/CD pipeline is a cornerstone of MLOps. It allows you to automate the process of building, testing, and deploying your application, which makes the process much faster, more reliable, and more repeatable.
Incorrect: This is the opposite of a good MLOps practice. MLOps is all about collaboration and shared responsibility between the development, operations, and data science teams.
Incorrect: This is a risky and an error-prone practice. A key goal of MLOps is to automate the deployment process.
questions.explanation: MLOps is a set of practices that aims to bring the discipline and the rigor of DevOps to the world of machine learning. For a RAG application, the two most important MLOps best practices are to use version control for everything and to automate your testing and deployment with a CI/CD pipeline. By using version control for your code, your prompts, and your other assets, you can ensure that your application is reproducible and that you have a clear audit trail of all changes. By using a CI/CD pipeline, you can create a fast, reliable, and repeatable process for getting your application from development to production.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that have a final answer that is a single word or a short phrase. For example, 'What is the name of the CEO of company X?' Which of the following is the best architecture for this?
answers: A simple RAG chain that retrieves the relevant document and then uses a prompt that is specifically designed for 'extractive question answering'.
An agent-based architecture with a web search tool.
A RAG system that uses a fine-tuned LLM.
A summarization-based RAG system.
feedbacks: Correct: Extractive question answering is the task of extracting a short text span from a document that answers a question. A simple RAG chain with a prompt that is optimized for this task is a very effective and efficient architecture.
Incorrect: A web search tool would be helpful if the information is not in the local knowledge base, but the core architecture for this task is still an extractive RAG chain.
Incorrect: While fine-tuning could improve the performance, it is not strictly necessary. A standard foundation model can perform extractive question answering very well with the right prompt.
Incorrect: Summarization is for generating a long-form summary of a document, not for extracting a short, factual answer.
questions.explanation: When the goal of a RAG application is to extract a short, factual answer from a set of documents, the best architecture is an 'extractive' RAG chain. This is a simple RAG pipeline where the final prompt is specifically designed to instruct the LLM to find and to extract the specific text span from the provided context that answers the user's question. This is a very common and effective pattern, and it is much more efficient than using a more complex architecture like an agent or a fine-tuned model.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them. They have a limited budget and want to use the most cost-effective solution. Which of the following is the most cost-effective approach on Databricks?
