Hosting a small, efficient open-source embedding model on a CPU-based Databricks Model Serving endpoint.
Using a large, GPU-accelerated cluster to process the embeddings as quickly as possible.
Using the most powerful foundation model API available on Databricks.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is likely to be the most expensive option.
Correct: For cost-sensitive applications, a small but effective open-source model running on a CPU-based endpoint can be a very cost-effective solution.
Incorrect: While this would be fast, it would also be very expensive.
Incorrect: The most powerful models are also the most expensive.
questions.explanation: When cost is the primary concern for an embedding pipeline, the best approach is to use a small and efficient open-source model and to host it on a CPU-based serving endpoint. There are a number of excellent open-source embedding models that are small enough to run efficiently on CPUs. By hosting one of these models on a Databricks Model Serving endpoint, you can get a scalable and reliable embedding solution at a very low cost. While this approach might not provide the absolute highest quality embeddings, it is often a very good trade-off for cost-sensitive applications.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to set up a system to automatically detect regressions in its performance. Which of the following is the best way to do this?
answers: Having the development team manually test the application every day.
Setting up a continuous evaluation pipeline that runs a set of 'golden' test cases against the application on a regular basis and compares the results to a set of expected outcomes.
Asking users to report any problems they encounter.
Assuming that the application will never have any regressions.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not an automated or a scalable solution.

Correct: This is the standard and most effective way to automatically detect regressions. By having a fixed set of test cases and expected outcomes, you can quickly identify any changes in the application's behavior.
Incorrect: While user feedback is valuable, it is a reactive, not a proactive, way to detect regressions.
Incorrect: All software has the potential for regressions, and it's important to have a system in place to detect them.
questions.explanation: To automatically detect regressions in a RAG application, you need to have a continuous evaluation pipeline that is based on a fixed set of test cases. This set of test cases, often called a 'golden dataset' or a 'regression suite', should cover the key capabilities of your application. The pipeline will then run these test cases against the application on a regular basis (e.g., every night, or after every code change) and will compare the results to a set of known-good, expected outcomes. If there are any differences, the pipeline can automatically raise an alert, notifying the team that a regression has occurred. This is a fundamental practice for maintaining the quality of a production AI system.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to manage the dependencies for the application (e.g., the specific versions of the Python libraries) in a consistent and a repeatable way. Which of the following is the best way to do this?
answers: Having each developer install the dependencies on their own machine.
Using a `requirements.txt` file to specify the dependencies and storing this file in a version control system along with the application's code.
Writing down the list of dependencies in a text document and emailing it to the team.
Using the newest version of all the libraries.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This will lead to inconsistencies and will not be repeatable.
Correct: This is the standard and best practice for managing Python dependencies. It provides a declarative, version-controlled, and repeatable way to manage the environment for the application.
Incorrect: This is not a reliable or a repeatable way to manage dependencies.
Incorrect: This can be risky, as the newest versions may have bugs or breaking changes. It's better to pin the specific versions of the libraries that are known to work with your application.
questions.explanation: Consistent and repeatable dependency management is a cornerstone of reliable software development. For a Python-based RAG application, the best way to achieve this is to use a `requirements.txt` file. This file lists all the libraries that the application depends on, along with their specific versions. By storing this file in a version control system alongside the application's code, you create a single source of truth for the application's environment. This makes it easy for any developer to create a consistent environment, and it makes the application's deployment process much more reliable and repeatable.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and has a requirement that all the data, both at rest and in transit, must be encrypted. Which TWO of the following are the most important ways that Databricks helps to meet this requirement?
answers: Databricks automatically encrypts all data stored in Delta Lake and in DBFS.
Databricks automatically encrypts all network traffic between the components of the platform and between the platform and the user.
Databricks provides a tool for users to manually encrypt their data before uploading it.
Databricks requires users to use a VPN for all connections.
feedbacks: Correct: Data at rest on Databricks is always encrypted by default.
Correct: Data in transit on Databricks is always encrypted using industry-standard protocols like TLS.
Incorrect: While users can do this, Databricks provides automatic encryption, which is much more secure and reliable.
Incorrect: While a VPN can add another layer of security, it is not required, as the standard connections to Databricks are already encrypted.
questions.explanation: Data encryption is a fundamental security requirement for any enterprise application. The Databricks platform is designed to be secure by default, and it provides automatic encryption for both data at rest and data in transit. All data that is stored in Delta Lake or in the Databricks File System (DBFS) is automatically encrypted at the storage layer. All network traffic, both within the Databricks platform and between the platform and the end-user, is encrypted using strong, industry-standard protocols like TLS. This comprehensive, built-in encryption provides a strong foundation for building secure RAG applications.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain application and wants to create a chain that takes a user's question, retrieves a set of documents, and then passes both the question and the documents to an LLM. Which of the following is the best way to structure the input to the final LLM call?
answers: Concatenating the question and the documents into a single long string.
Using a dictionary with two keys: 'question' and 'context', where the 'context' is the string of retrieved documents.
Creating a prompt template that has two input variables: `question` and `context`.
Passing the question and the documents as two separate arguments to the LLM's `predict` method.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While possible, this does not provide a clear separation between the question and the context, which can make it harder for the LLM.

Correct: This is the standard and best practice. By passing a structured dictionary with clear keys for the question and the context, you make the prompt much clearer and easier for the LLM to understand.

Correct: This is the other half of the solution. The dictionary from the previous step is passed to a prompt template that is designed to format the question and the context into a clear and effective prompt for the LLM.
Incorrect: The `predict` method of an LLM in LangChain typically takes a single string as input. You need to use a prompt template to combine the question and the context into a single string.
questions.explanation: The way that you structure the prompt is a critical factor in the performance of a RAG application. The best practice is to use a prompt template that has separate input variables for the user's question and the retrieved context. This allows you to create a very clear and well-structured prompt that makes it easy for the LLM to understand its task. The input to this prompt template would then be a dictionary with the keys 'question' and 'context'. This structured approach to prompt engineering is a key part of building a high-quality and a reliable RAG application.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large set of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is based on the logical structure of the documents (e.g., paragraphs). Which of the following is the best tool for this?
answers: A simple Python script that splits the text by the newline character (`\n`).

A recursive character text splitter that is configured to split by a sequence of separators, such as `

` (for paragraphs), then `
` (for lines), and then spaces.
A fixed-size chunker.
A tokenizer from a pre-trained language model.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this might work for some documents, a double newline is a more reliable way to split by paragraphs.
Correct: A recursive character text splitter is the perfect tool for this. It allows you to define a hierarchy of separators that corresponds to the logical structure of your documents.
Incorrect: A fixed-size chunker is not aware of the logical structure of the document.
Incorrect: A tokenizer splits the text into words or sub-words, not into larger chunks like paragraphs.
questions.explanation:
When you want to create chunks that align with the logical structure of your documents, a recursive character text splitter is the best tool for the job. You can configure it with a list of separators, and it will try to split the text using the first separator in the list. If the resulting chunks are still too large, it will then try the next separator in the list, and so on. By providing a list of separators that corresponds to the logical structure of your documents (e.g., `['

', '
', ' ']`), you can create a very effective and a very robust chunking strategy.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to ensure that they can monitor the application for both operational issues (like latency and errors) and for quality issues (like hallucinations). Which TWO Databricks features provide the most comprehensive solution for this?
answers: Databricks Model Serving, which provides the infrastructure for deploying the application.
Databricks Lakehouse Monitoring, which can track both operational metrics (like request volume) and data/quality metrics (like drift and outlier detection).
Inference tables, which log all the requests and responses to the serving endpoint, providing the raw data needed for both operational and quality monitoring.
The MLflow Model Registry.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While Model Serving is the deployment platform, it is not the monitoring solution itself.
Correct: Lakehouse Monitoring is a purpose-built solution for monitoring both the operational health and the quality of data and AI assets.
Correct: Inference tables are the foundational data source for all monitoring. They contain the data needed to calculate latency, error rates, faithfulness, and any other metric you want to track.
Incorrect: The Model Registry is for managing the lifecycle of models, not for real-time monitoring.
questions.explanation: For a comprehensive monitoring solution for a RAG application on Databricks, you need to use a combination of inference tables and Lakehouse Monitoring. Inference tables provide the raw, detailed data about every single request and response. This data is the ground truth that you can use for any kind of analysis, from debugging a specific error to calculating high-level quality metrics. Lakehouse Monitoring provides a higher-level, managed solution that can automatically track key metrics over time, can detect drift and anomalies, and can provide dashboards and alerts. By using these two features together, you can get a complete, 360-degree view of the health and the quality of your RAG application.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and is using a prompt that asks the LLM to both answer the user's question and to provide a confidence score for its answer. What is the best way to parse the output of the LLM to get both the answer and the confidence score as separate fields?
answers: Using a regular expression to try to find the answer and the score in the LLM's text output.
Using a LangChain Output Parser that is configured with a Pydantic model that has two fields: `answer` (a string) and `confidence_score` (a float).
Asking the LLM to output a JSON object with the two fields and then parsing the JSON string.
Simply taking the entire text output of the LLM as the answer and ignoring the confidence score.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be very brittle and would be likely to fail if the LLM formats its output in a slightly different way.

Correct: This is the most robust and the most reliable way to get structured output from an LLM. By defining the desired output structure with a Pydantic model, you can use an output parser to automatically extract the information into a clean, structured object.

Correct: This is another very good approach. Most LLMs are very good at generating JSON. You can then use a standard JSON parser to get the structured data. This is often used in conjunction with a JSON output parser from LangChain for added robustness.
Incorrect: This would not meet the requirement of getting both the answer and the confidence score as separate fields.
questions.explanation: When you need to get multiple, distinct pieces of information from an LLM's response, you need a way to get structured output. The two best ways to do this are to use a Pydantic output parser or to ask for a JSON object. A Pydantic output parser is a very powerful and 'LangChain-native' way to do this. You define the desired output structure as a Python class, and the parser handles the rest. Asking the LLM to output a JSON object is another very effective technique. LLMs are generally very good at generating well-formed JSON, and you can then easily parse this JSON to get the structured data you need.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a set of documents that are stored in a variety of character encodings (e.g., UTF-8, ASCII, ISO-8859-1). Which of the following is the most important pre-processing step to perform on this data?
answers: Converting all the documents to a single, standard character encoding, such as UTF-8.
Choosing the character encoding that is used by the majority of the documents and ignoring the rest.
Assuming that all the downstream tools will be able to handle the mix of encodings.
Compressing all the documents to save space.
feedbacks: Correct: Before you can do any text processing, you need to ensure that all your text is in a single, consistent character encoding. UTF-8 is the modern standard and is almost always the best choice.
Incorrect: This would result in the loss of data from the documents that use a different encoding.
Incorrect: This is a very risky assumption and is likely to lead to errors and corrupted data.
Incorrect: Compression does not address the issue of character encoding.
questions.explanation: Working with text data from multiple sources often means dealing with multiple character encodings. The first and most critical step in any text processing pipeline is to normalize all the text to a single, standard encoding. UTF-8 is the universal standard for text encoding and is the best choice for this. By converting all your documents to UTF-8 at the very beginning of your pipeline, you can avoid a wide range of potential issues and can ensure that all your downstream tools will be able to process the text correctly.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by its human resources department to answer questions about employee data. The application will have access to highly sensitive PII. Which of the following is the most important security control to implement?
answers: A user-friendly and intuitive user interface.
A robust and fine-grained access control system, based on the principle of least privilege, to ensure that HR employees can only access the data that they are explicitly authorized to see.
A high-performance LLM to ensure that the answers are generated quickly.
A comprehensive set of unit tests for the application's code.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While important for usability, this is not a security control.

Correct: For an application that handles sensitive PII, a strong access control system is the most critical security control. The principle of least privilege dictates that users should only have access to the bare minimum of data that they need to perform their jobs. Unity Catalog is the tool to implement this on Databricks.
Incorrect: Performance is not a security control.
Incorrect: While unit tests are a good software engineering practice, they are not the most important security control for protecting sensitive data.
questions.explanation: When an application handles sensitive personally identifiable information (PII), the single most important security control is a robust access control system. This system must be based on the principle of least privilege, which means that users are only given access to the specific data that they absolutely need to do their job. In the context of a RAG application for an HR department, this might mean that an HR generalist can only see the data for the employees in their assigned business unit. On Databricks, this kind of fine-grained access control can be implemented using Unity Catalog.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain agent that needs to be able to have a conversation with the user and to remember the context of the conversation. Which TWO of the following LangChain components are essential for this?
answers: The `AgentExecutor`.
A `PromptTemplate` that includes a placeholder for the `chat_history`.
A `VectorStoreRetriever`.
An `OutputParser`.
feedbacks: Correct: The `AgentExecutor` is the runtime for an agent. It is responsible for calling the agent's LLM, for parsing its output, and for executing the chosen tools. It also manages the memory of the conversation.
Correct: The prompt is the key to making the memory work. It must include a placeholder where the history of the conversation can be injected, so that the LLM has the context of the previous turns.
Incorrect: A retriever is for fetching documents and is not a core component of conversational memory.
Incorrect: While an agent uses an output parser to understand the LLM's response, the memory itself is managed by the `AgentExecutor` and is passed to the LLM through the prompt.
questions.explanation: To create a conversational agent in LangChain, you need two key components: the `AgentExecutor` and a prompt that is designed for conversation. The `AgentExecutor` is the engine that drives the agent. It manages the loop of calling the LLM, executing tools, and updating the conversation's memory. The prompt is what makes the agent aware of the conversation's history. By including a placeholder for the `chat_history` in the prompt, you ensure that on every turn, the LLM has the full context of the conversation so far, which allows it to generate a coherent and a relevant response.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is both semantically aware and that produces chunks of a relatively uniform size. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Sentence-level chunking.
Semantic chunking, with a post-processing step to merge or to split the chunks to meet a target size range.
Recursive character text splitting, with the separators chosen to align with the semantic structure of the documents.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This strategy is not semantically aware.
Incorrect: This can produce chunks of very different sizes.
Correct: This is a powerful, hybrid approach. You first use semantic chunking to get semantically coherent chunks, and then you apply a second step to normalize their size.

Correct: A well-configured recursive splitter is often a very good approximation of a semantic chunking strategy. By choosing the right separators, you can create chunks that are both semantically meaningful and reasonably uniform in size.
questions.explanation: Getting chunks that are both semantically coherent and uniform in size is often the 'holy grail' of chunking. The two best strategies for this are to use a hybrid semantic chunking approach or to use a well-configured recursive character text splitter. The hybrid semantic approach is a two-step process: first, you use a semantic chunker to find the natural breaking points in the text, and then you have a second step that merges or splits those initial chunks to get them into a desired size range. A recursive character text splitter can often achieve a similar result in a single step. By carefully choosing the hierarchy of separators, you can design a chunking strategy that respects the semantic structure of the text while also producing chunks that are of a consistent size.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and is using an LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate its performance. They are getting a single score for each response from the judge. They now want to be able to see the trend of this score over time. Which of the following is the best way to do this?
answers: Logging the score for each evaluation run to a Delta table and then creating a Databricks Dashboard to visualize the trend.
Printing the score to the console at the end of each evaluation run.
Logging the scores as a metric in an MLflow experiment.
Storing the scores in a Python list in the evaluation script.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a robust and a flexible solution. By logging the scores to a Delta table, you create a persistent record of the evaluation results. A Databricks Dashboard can then be used to create a rich and an interactive visualization of the performance trend.
Incorrect: This would not be a persistent or a scalable way to track the scores over time.

Correct: This is another excellent option. MLflow is designed for tracking metrics over time, and its UI provides a powerful interface for visualizing and for comparing the performance of different runs.
Incorrect: This would not be a persistent solution, and the data would be lost when the script finishes.
questions.explanation: Once you have a way to score your RAG application's responses, you need a way to track that score over time. On Databricks, the two best ways to do this are to use a Delta table with a dashboard or to use MLflow. Logging the scores to a Delta table and then building a dashboard gives you a lot of flexibility to create custom visualizations and to share the results with a wide audience. Using MLflow is a great choice if you want to integrate the evaluation into a more formal MLOps workflow. The MLflow UI is purpose-built for tracking and for comparing metrics from different experiment runs.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by its finance team to analyze confidential financial reports. They have a multi-select requirement for TWO of the most critical security and governance features for this application.
answers: The ability to fine-tune the LLM for a more financial-specific tone.
The use of end-to-end encryption for all data, both at rest and in transit.

A fine-grained access control system that can be integrated with the company's existing user directory (like Azure Active Directory) to ensure that only authorized finance team members can access the application and its data.
A feature that allows the users to share the application's responses on social media.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a quality feature, not a security or a governance feature.
Correct: For an application that handles sensitive financial data, end-to-end encryption is a non-negotiable security requirement.

Correct: A robust access control system that is integrated with the company's identity management system is another critical security feature. This ensures that the access policies are consistent and are easy to manage.
Incorrect: This would be a major security risk and would be the opposite of what you would want for a confidential application.
questions.explanation: For a high-security application that handles confidential financial data, a defense-in-depth approach to security and governance is required. Two of the most critical components of this are end-to-end encryption and a robust, integrated access control system. End-to-end encryption ensures that the data is protected from unauthorized access at all times. An integrated access control system ensures that only the right people have access to the application and its data, and that their permissions are managed in a centralized and a consistent way.

questions.question: A developer is building a LangChain application and wants to create a RAG chain that first retrieves documents and then passes them to an LLM. However, they only want to pass the content of the documents to the LLM, not the metadata. Which of the following is the best way to do this in LCEL?
answers: `retriever | llm`
`retriever | (lambda docs: [d.page_content for d in docs]) | llm`
`retriever | {'context': lambda docs: [d.page_content for d in docs]} | prompt | llm`
The retriever should be configured to only return the content of the documents.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would pass the entire `Document` objects, including the metadata, to the LLM.

Correct: This is a common and an effective pattern. You can use a `RunnableLambda` (which can be expressed as a simple lambda function) to transform the output of the retriever. In this case, the lambda function iterates through the list of `Document` objects and extracts the `page_content` from each.
Incorrect: This is overly complex. You can perform the transformation in a simpler way.
Incorrect: Most retrievers in LangChain return a list of `Document` objects, which include both the content and the metadata. You typically need to perform a transformation step after the retrieval.
questions.explanation: LangChain Expression Language (LCEL) is designed to be highly composable, and a key part of this is the ability to easily transform the data as it flows through the chain. A common use case in a RAG pipeline is to extract just the text content from the `Document` objects that are returned by the retriever. The most idiomatic and a very powerful way to do this is to use a `RunnableLambda` (which can be written as a simple Python lambda function). By inserting this lambda function into the chain after the retriever, you can easily transform the list of `Document` objects into a list of strings, which can then be passed to the next step in the chain.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that are in a clean, plain text format. They want to use a chunking strategy that is simple, fast, and that respects sentence boundaries. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Semantic chunking.
Sentence-level chunking, using a library like NLTK or spaCy to split the text into sentences.
Recursive character text splitting.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This strategy does not respect sentence boundaries.
Incorrect: This is a more complex strategy and is not necessary for this simple use case.

Correct: For clean, plain text, a sentence-level chunker is often the perfect choice. It's simple, it's fast, and it does a good job of creating semantically coherent chunks by ensuring that sentences are not broken up.
Incorrect: While this could be configured to work, a dedicated sentence-level chunker is a more direct and a more semantically aware tool for this specific task.
questions.explanation: When your source documents are clean, plain text, and your goal is to create chunks that correspond to sentences, the best tool for the job is a dedicated sentence-level chunker. Libraries like NLTK and spaCy have highly optimized and accurate sentence tokenizers that can quickly and reliably split a document into a list of its constituent sentences. This is a very common and a very effective chunking strategy for a wide range of RAG applications.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to compare the performance of their current production version with a new experimental version. They want to do this in a live production environment. Which of the following is the best way to conduct this comparison?
answers: Deploying the new version to all users and then asking them if they like it better.

Conducting an A/B test, where a portion of the user traffic is randomly routed to the new version and the rest is routed to the old version. The performance of the two versions can then be compared on a set of key metrics.
Deploying the new version to a separate staging environment and testing it there.
Showing both answers to the user and asking them to choose the better one.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be a risky and an unscientific way to compare the two versions.
Correct: An A/B test is the gold standard for comparing two versions of an application in a live environment. It provides a scientifically rigorous way to measure the impact of the changes.
Incorrect: While testing in a staging environment is a good practice, it does not tell you how the new version will perform with real users and real traffic. An A/B test is needed for that.
Incorrect: This is a form of user feedback, but it's not a standard A/B test. A standard A/B test is 'blind' to the user.
questions.explanation: When you want to compare two versions of an application in a live production environment, the best and the most rigorous way to do it is with an A/B test. In an A/B test, you randomly assign users to two groups: a control group that sees the old version of the application, and a treatment group that sees the new version. You then track a set of key metrics for both groups. By comparing the metrics between the two groups, you can get a statistically significant measure of the impact of the changes in the new version. This is a fundamental technique for data-driven product development.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by its sales team to quickly get information about their products. The sales team is often on the road and will be using the application from their mobile devices. Which TWO of the following are the most important design considerations for this application?
answers: The application should have a responsive user interface that works well on small screens.
The application should be optimized for low-latency responses, as mobile network connections can be slow and unreliable.
The application should have a very complex and a feature-rich interface.
The application should only be accessible when the user is connected to the company's corporate Wi-Fi network.
feedbacks: Correct: For a mobile-first application, a responsive UI is a critical requirement. The application must be easy to use on a phone or a tablet.
Correct: Mobile users are often impatient and are on less reliable networks. It's crucial that the application is as fast and as responsive as possible.
Incorrect: For a mobile application, simplicity and ease of use are usually more important than having a large number of features.
Incorrect: This would make the application useless for a sales team that is on the road.
questions.explanation: When you are designing an application for a mobile workforce, the two most important design considerations are the user interface and the performance. The user interface must be responsive, meaning that it can adapt to the small screen size of a mobile device and can provide a good user experience. The performance of the application is also critical. The application should be designed to be as fast and as lightweight as possible, to provide a snappy, low-latency experience even on a slow or an unreliable mobile network connection.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that are a mix of simple factual questions and more complex, multi-step questions. Which of the following is the best architecture for this?
answers: A single, simple RAG chain.

An agent-based architecture that can use a simple RAG chain as one of its tools. The agent can then decide to use the simple RAG tool for the factual questions, and can use its other tools and its reasoning capabilities for the more complex questions.
A system that tries to classify the question first and then routes it to either a simple RAG chain or a more complex agent.
A system that always uses the most complex agent architecture, even for the simple questions.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A simple RAG chain would not be able to handle the complex, multi-step questions.
Correct: This is a powerful and a flexible architecture. It uses a simple RAG chain for what it's good at, and it uses the power of an agent for the more complex tasks.

Correct: This is another excellent architecture. By putting a 'router' in front of the application, you can intelligently send the user's query to the system that is best equipped to handle it. This can be more efficient than using a single, large agent for all questions.
Incorrect: This would be inefficient and would likely result in a higher latency and a higher cost for the simple questions.
questions.explanation: When an application needs to handle a mix of simple and complex questions, a hybrid architecture is often the best approach. There are two great ways to build such an architecture. The first is to use an agent that has a simple RAG chain as one of its tools. The agent can then learn to use this simple tool for the simple questions. The second approach is to build an explicit 'router' that first classifies the user's question and then sends it to the appropriate backend system (either a simple RAG chain or a more complex agent). Both of these architectures provide a powerful and an efficient way to handle a wide range of user queries.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create a vector index. They have a requirement that the index must be updated in near real-time as new documents are added to the source. Which of the following is the best solution on Databricks?
answers: A DIRECT index in Databricks Vector Search.
A DELTA_SYNC index in Databricks Vector Search, with the source being a Delta table that is updated by a continuous Delta Live Tables pipeline.
A batch job that runs once a day to re-index the entire dataset.
A custom streaming application that uses a third-party vector database.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A DIRECT index is for static data and is not updated in real-time.

Correct: This is the state-of-the-art solution for real-time RAG on Databricks. The continuous DLT pipeline provides low-latency ingestion of the new data, and the DELTA_SYNC index ensures that the vector store is updated in near real-time.
Incorrect: This would not meet the requirement for near real-time updates.
Incorrect: While this is a possible solution, the combination of DLT and Databricks Vector Search is a much more integrated and a much more managed solution on the Databricks platform.
questions.explanation: For a RAG application that requires near real-time updates, you need an end-to-end streaming data pipeline. On Databricks, the best way to build this is to use a combination of Delta Live Tables and Databricks Vector Search. You would first create a Delta Live Tables pipeline that is configured to run in 'continuous' mode. This pipeline would ingest the new documents from a streaming source (like Kafka or Kinesis) and would write them to a Delta table with very low latency. You would then create a Databricks Vector Search index in `DELTA_SYNC` mode that uses this Delta table as its source. This will ensure that as soon as a new document lands in the Delta table, it is automatically and almost instantaneously indexed and is made available to your RAG application.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to track the 'faithfulness' of its responses. They do not have a large, human-labeled dataset for this. Which of the following is the most effective and scalable way to measure faithfulness in this scenario?
answers: Manually reviewing every single response from the application.
Using an LLM-as-a-judge.
Assuming that all the answers are faithful.
Calculating the semantic similarity between the generated answer and the retrieved context.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be scalable for any real-world application.

Correct: This is the most effective and a very scalable way to measure faithfulness without a human-labeled dataset. You can use a powerful LLM to compare the generated answer to the retrieved context and to determine if the answer is factually supported.
Incorrect: This is a dangerous assumption, as all LLMs can hallucinate.

Correct: This is another good, automated approach. You can use an embedding model to calculate the semantic similarity between the answer and the context. A low similarity score can be a good indicator that the answer is not well-grounded in the context.
questions.explanation: Measuring the faithfulness of a RAG application is crucial for building a trustworthy system. When you don't have a large, human-labeled dataset, you need to use automated techniques. The two best techniques for this are to use an LLM-as-a-judge and to calculate the semantic similarity between the answer and the context. The LLM-as-a-judge approach is very powerful, as it can provide a nuanced, human-like judgment of faithfulness. The semantic similarity approach is a simpler, more quantitative method that can also be a very effective signal. A good evaluation pipeline will often use a combination of both of these techniques.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application and wants to use a CI/CD pipeline to automate the deployment process. The application consists of a set of Python notebooks and a RAG chain that is logged as an MLflow model. Which TWO of the following are the key steps in a CI/CD pipeline for this application?
answers: When a developer pushes a change to the code, a job is automatically triggered that runs a set of automated tests on the application.

If the tests pass, the pipeline automatically promotes the new version of the MLflow model to the 'production' stage in the Model Registry and then updates the production model serving endpoint to use this new version.
Manually running the notebooks in the production workspace after a code change.
Emailing the new version of the notebooks to the operations team and asking them to deploy it.
feedbacks: Correct: Automated testing is a core part of CI (Continuous Integration). Every change should be automatically tested to ensure that it doesn't break anything.
Correct: This is the CD (Continuous Deployment) part of the pipeline. If the new version of the application passes all the tests, the pipeline can automatically deploy it to production.
Incorrect: This is a manual process and is the opposite of what a CI/CD pipeline does.
Incorrect: A CI/CD pipeline is designed to eliminate these kinds of manual handoffs.
questions.explanation: A CI/CD pipeline is a key enabler for a fast, reliable, and a repeatable deployment process. For a RAG application on Databricks, a typical CI/CD pipeline would have two main stages. The first is the Continuous Integration (CI) stage, where any new code change automatically triggers a set of automated tests. This ensures that all changes are validated before they are merged into the main branch. The second is the Continuous Deployment (CD) stage. If the tests pass, the pipeline can then automatically deploy the new version of the application. For a RAG application, this would typically involve promoting the new version of the MLflow model to the 'production' stage and then updating the production model serving endpoint to use this new version.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and is trying to decide on the right architecture. The application needs to be able to answer questions that may require information from either a set of documents or from a web search. Which of the following is the best architecture for this?
answers: A simple RAG chain that only has access to the local set of documents.
A LangChain agent that has two tools: a `VectorStoreRetriever` for searching the local documents, and a `WebSearchTool` for searching the web.
A RAG chain that always performs a web search for every question.
A RAG chain that first searches the local documents, and if it doesn't find an answer, then it performs a web search.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not be able to answer questions that require a web search.

Correct: This is the perfect architecture for this use case. The agent can use the LLM's reasoning capabilities to decide whether to search the local documents or the web, based on the user's question.
Incorrect: This would be inefficient and unnecessary for questions that can be answered from the local documents.

Correct: This is another good architecture, often called a 'fallback' or a 'cascade' pattern. It's a simpler and a more deterministic approach than a full agent, and it can be very effective for this kind of use case.
questions.explanation: When a RAG application needs to be able to get information from multiple different sources, you need an architecture that can intelligently choose the right source for the right question. The two best architectures for this are an agent-based system and a fallback chain. An agent is the more powerful and a more flexible solution. It can use the LLM's reasoning to decide which tool to use. A fallback chain is a simpler and a more deterministic approach. It tries the primary source first (e.g., the local documents), and if that fails to produce a good answer, it then falls back to the secondary source (e.g., a web search). Both are excellent patterns for building a more capable and a more robust RAG application.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them. They have a powerful GPU available and want to process the embeddings as quickly as possible. Which of the following is the most important consideration for maximizing the performance?
answers: Using a very small batch size.
Using a large batch size that is tuned to saturate the GPU's memory and compute resources without causing an out-of-memory error.
Running the embedding process on the CPU.
Using a single-threaded Python script to call the embedding model.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A small batch size will not fully utilize the parallel processing power of the GPU.
Correct: To get the maximum performance from a GPU, you need to feed it a large batch of data at once. The key is to find the largest batch size that will fit in the GPU's memory.
Incorrect: A GPU is orders of magnitude faster than a CPU for tasks like embedding generation.
Incorrect: A single-threaded script would not be able to keep the GPU busy. You need to use a framework that can efficiently feed the data to the GPU.
questions.explanation: Getting the maximum performance out of a GPU for a task like embedding generation is all about finding the right batch size. A GPU is a massively parallel processor, and to get its full benefit, you need to give it a lot of work to do at once. This means using a large batch size. The optimal batch size will depend on the specific GPU and the size of your model, but the general principle is to make it as large as possible without running out of the GPU's memory. By tuning the batch size to fully saturate the GPU, you can achieve a massive speedup compared to running on a CPU or using a small batch size.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to implement a system for catching regressions. They have created a 'golden dataset' of question-answer pairs. Which of the following is the most effective way to use this dataset to catch regressions?
answers: On a regular basis, run the application on the questions in the golden dataset and compare the generated answers to the golden answers. If the quality score drops below a certain threshold, raise an alert.
Manually check a few of the questions from the golden dataset whenever a developer feels like it.
Use the golden dataset to fine-tune the LLM.
Assume that since you have a golden dataset, no regressions will ever occur.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the standard and most effective way to use a golden dataset for regression testing. It provides an automated way to detect any degradation in the application's performance.
Incorrect: This is not a systematic or a reliable way to catch regressions.
Incorrect: While you could use the dataset for fine-tuning, its primary purpose in this context is for evaluation, not for training.
Incorrect: The golden dataset is a tool for detecting regressions, not for preventing them.
questions.explanation: A golden dataset is the cornerstone of a good regression testing strategy for a RAG application. The process is simple but powerful: on a regular basis (e.g., after every code change, or on a nightly schedule), you automatically run the application on the questions in your golden dataset. You then compare the answers generated by the application to the 'golden' answers in your dataset, using a set of automated metrics (like semantic similarity or an LLM-as-a-judge). If the scores for the new version of the application are significantly worse than the scores for the previous version, you can automatically trigger an alert to notify the development team that a regression has occurred. This provides a crucial safety net for the development process.

questions.question: A company is deploying a RAG application that will be used by hundreds of concurrent users. They need to ensure that the application is both scalable and cost-effective. Which of the following is the most important feature of Databricks Model Serving for achieving this?
answers: The ability to serve any Python model.
The auto-scaling capability, which can automatically scale the number of model replicas up and down based on the request load.
The integration with Unity Catalog for governance.
The ability to view the logs of the model endpoint.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this is a key feature, it is not the most important one for scalability and cost-effectiveness.

Correct: Auto-scaling is the key to building a scalable and a cost-effective serving solution. It ensures that you have enough capacity to handle peak load, while also ensuring that you are not paying for idle resources during off-peak times.
Incorrect: While important for security, this is not the key feature for scalability and cost-effectiveness.
Incorrect: While useful for debugging, this is not the key feature for scalability and cost-effectiveness.
questions.explanation: For a production application with a variable workload, auto-scaling is an essential feature. Databricks Model Serving's auto-scaling capability is the key to building a RAG application that is both highly scalable and cost-effective. It works by automatically monitoring the request load on your serving endpoint and by adjusting the number of active model replicas to match the demand. When the traffic is high, it will scale up the number of replicas to ensure that the application remains responsive. When the traffic is low, it will scale down the number of replicas to save money. This 'pay-for-what-you-use' model is the most efficient way to serve a production AI application.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them. They have a limited amount of time and want to use the fastest possible solution. Which of the following is the best approach on Databricks?
answers: Using a small, CPU-based cluster to process the documents one by one.
Using a large, GPU-accelerated cluster and a Pandas UDF to process the documents in large batches.
Using a foundation model API from a third-party provider.
Loading all the documents onto a single, powerful machine and processing them there.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be the slowest possible solution.
Correct: For maximum speed, you need to use a combination of distributed processing (with a large Spark cluster) and GPU acceleration. A Pandas UDF is the key to unlocking this performance.
Incorrect: While convenient, calling an external API will introduce network latency and will likely not be as fast as a highly optimized, local solution on a large GPU cluster.
Incorrect: While a single, powerful machine can be fast, for a very large dataset, a distributed approach on a cluster will almost always be faster.
questions.explanation: When raw speed is the top priority for an embedding pipeline, you need to bring as much hardware to bear on the problem as possible. On Databricks, the fastest possible solution is to use a large, GPU-accelerated Spark cluster. You would use Spark to distribute the processing of the documents across all the nodes in the cluster, and you would use a Pandas UDF to apply the embedding model in large batches on the GPUs of the worker nodes. This massively parallel approach is the state-of-the-art for high-performance, large-scale embedding generation.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to get both a quantitative and a qualitative measure of its performance. Which of the following pairs of evaluation techniques would provide this?
answers: Measuring the latency of the responses and the throughput of the serving endpoint.
Calculating the ROUGE score of the responses and the number of tokens in the responses.
Using an LLM-as-a-judge to get a numerical score for faithfulness, and also conducting user interviews to get open-ended feedback.
Manually reviewing a sample of the responses and also conducting a usability test.
feedbacks: Incorrect: These are both quantitative, operational metrics.
Incorrect: These are both quantitative, quality-related metrics.

Correct: This is a perfect combination. The LLM-as-a-judge provides a scalable, quantitative measure of a key quality metric. The user interviews provide deep, rich, qualitative insights into the user experience.
Incorrect: These are both qualitative techniques.
questions.explanation: A comprehensive evaluation plan should always include a mix of quantitative and qualitative methods. The quantitative methods give you the 'what' (e.g., 'our faithfulness score is 0.85'), and the qualitative methods give you the 'why' (e.g., 'users are confused by the way the application presents its sources'). A great combination for a RAG application is to use an LLM-as-a-judge to get a scalable, quantitative measure of a metric like faithfulness, and to also conduct a set of user interviews or usability tests to get a deep, qualitative understanding of the user experience. The combination of these two types of feedback is incredibly powerful and is the key to building a truly great application.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that will be robust to a wide variety of document types and structures. Which of the following is the best general-purpose chunking strategy?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Sentence-level chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
Semantic chunking.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a robust strategy, as it does not respect the semantic structure of the documents.
Incorrect: This can be a good strategy, but it can struggle with documents that have very long or very short sentences.

Correct: A recursive character text splitter is an excellent general-purpose chunking strategy. It's robust, it's easy to configure, and it does a good job of respecting the semantic structure of the text by trying to split on larger boundaries (like paragraphs) before resorting to smaller ones.

Incorrect: While very powerful, semantic chunking is more complex and computationally expensive than recursive splitting, so it might not be the best choice for a 'general-purpose' strategy where simplicity and speed are also important.
questions.explanation: When you need a good, general-purpose chunking strategy that will work well on a wide variety of documents, a recursive character text splitter is almost always the best choice. It provides a great balance of simplicity, performance, and quality. By defining a hierarchy of separators (e.g., paragraphs, then sentences, then words), you can create a chunking strategy that is robust to different document structures and that does a good job of creating semantically coherent chunks. It's the 'Swiss Army knife' of chunking and is a great place to start for almost any RAG application.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application that will be used by multiple teams. They want to ensure that the AI assets for the application (like the models and the prompts) are governed in a way that is consistent with how they govern their data. Which Databricks feature is designed to provide this unified governance?
answers: Databricks Model Serving.
Unity Catalog.
MLflow.
Databricks SQL.

Correct: Unity Catalog is the unified governance solution for all data and AI assets on the Databricks platform. It allows you to manage your models and prompts with the same tools and the same policies that you use for your data.
Incorrect: While MLflow is a key part of the MLOps workflow, Unity Catalog is the overarching governance layer.
Incorrect: Databricks SQL is for analytics, not for governance.
questions.explanation: The key to unified governance for data and AI on Databricks is Unity Catalog. It provides a single, centralized catalog for all your data and AI assets, including tables, files, models, and prompts. This allows you to apply a single, consistent set of governance policies (for things like access control and data lineage) across all your assets. This unified approach is essential for large organizations that want to manage their AI development in a secure, a compliant, and a consistent way.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large set of documents and wants to use a chunking strategy that is based on the semantic meaning of the text, rather than on its syntactic structure. Which of the following is the best choice?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Sentence-level chunking.
Semantic chunking.
Recursive character text splitting.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a purely syntactic strategy.
Incorrect: This is also a syntactic strategy.

Correct: Semantic chunking is a modern technique that uses an embedding model to find the natural semantic breaks in the text. It is the only chunking strategy that is based on the meaning of the text, rather than on its structure.
Incorrect: This is a sophisticated syntactic strategy, but it is not a semantic one.
questions.explanation: For the highest quality, most semantically coherent chunks, the best strategy is semantic chunking. Unlike all other common chunking strategies, which rely on the syntactic structure of the text (like characters, sentences, or paragraphs), semantic chunking uses an embedding model to understand the meaning of the text. It identifies the points where the topic of the text shifts and creates chunks that correspond to these semantic units. This can lead to a significant improvement in the quality of the RAG system, as the chunks are much more likely to represent a single, coherent thought or idea.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and has set up a continuous evaluation pipeline. The pipeline runs a set of golden test cases every night and logs the results to an MLflow experiment. How can the team be automatically notified if there is a regression in the performance?
answers: By having a team member manually check the MLflow UI every morning.
By using the MLflow REST API to query the results of the latest run and to send an email or a Slack notification if the metrics are below a certain threshold.
By configuring a job in Databricks that runs after the evaluation job and that checks the metrics of the last run. This job can be configured to send an alert on failure.
By assuming that MLflow will automatically send an alert if there is a regression.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not an automated solution.
Correct: The MLflow API provides programmatic access to all the data in MLflow. You can use this API to build a custom alerting solution that integrates with your existing notification systems.

Correct: This is another excellent and a very common pattern. You can create a simple 'downstream' job that is responsible for checking the results of the main evaluation job and for sending an alert if there is a problem.
Incorrect: MLflow does not have a built-in alerting feature. You need to build your own alerting logic on top of it.
questions.explanation: MLflow is a great tool for tracking the results of a continuous evaluation pipeline, but it doesn't have a built-in alerting mechanism. To get automatic notifications of a regression, you need to build your own alerting logic. The two best ways to do this are to use the MLflow API or to use a downstream Databricks job. You can write a script that uses the MLflow API to get the metrics from the latest evaluation run and that then sends an alert if there is a problem. Alternatively, you can create a second Databricks job that is triggered after the main evaluation job finishes. This second job's only purpose is to check the results of the first job and to send an alert if necessary.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to follow MLOps best practices. They want to automate the entire process of testing and deploying the application. This practice is known as:
answers: Agile development.
Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment (CI/CD).
Waterfall development.
Manual deployment.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While related, Agile is a general software development methodology. CI/CD is the specific practice of automating the deployment pipeline.

Correct: CI/CD is the cornerstone of modern MLOps. It's the practice of using automation to build, to test, and to deploy your application, which makes the process faster, more reliable, and more repeatable.
Incorrect: This is an older, sequential development methodology that is the opposite of the iterative approach enabled by CI/CD.
Incorrect: This is the opposite of CI/CD.
questions.explanation: The heart of MLOps is automation, and the key practice for automating the application lifecycle is Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD). Continuous Integration is the practice of automatically testing every change that is made to the code. Continuous Deployment is the practice of automatically deploying the application to production if it passes all the tests. By implementing a CI/CD pipeline, a company can significantly increase the speed and the reliability of their development process and can ensure that they are following modern MLOps best practices.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that will be used to answer questions about a company's financial results. The results are stored in a set of tables in a Delta Lake. Which of the following is the best way to get the information from these tables to answer a user's question?
answers: Converting the Delta tables to a set of text documents and using a standard RAG retriever.

Using a 'Text-to-SQL' agent that can take a user's natural language question, can convert it to a SQL query, can execute the query against the Delta tables, and can then use the results to generate an answer.
Fine-tuning the LLM on the contents of the Delta tables.
Asking the user to write their own SQL query.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would lose the valuable structure of the tables.

Correct: For structured data like that in a Delta table, a Text-to-SQL approach is the state-of-the-art. It allows the LLM to leverage the full power of the SQL query engine to get the precise information it needs.
Incorrect: This would not be an effective or an efficient way to query the data.
Incorrect: The goal of the application is to allow the user to ask questions in natural language.
questions.explanation: When the knowledge for a RAG application is stored in a structured format like a set of Delta tables, the best way to access that knowledge is with a Text-to-SQL agent. This type of agent uses the power of an LLM to bridge the gap between natural language and SQL. It can take a user's question, like 'What were our total sales in Q2?', and can automatically convert it into a valid SQL query that can be run against the Delta tables. The agent can then take the results of that query and can use them to generate a natural language answer for the user. This is a very powerful and a very effective way to build a RAG application on top of structured data.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them using a foundation model API. They want to do this in a way that is both scalable and that makes efficient use of the API. Which of the following is the best approach in Spark?
answers: Using a `for` loop to iterate through the rows of the Spark DataFrame and to call the API for each row.
Using a Pandas UDF.
Setting the batch size of the Pandas UDF to 1.
Tuning the batch size of the Pandas UDF to find the optimal balance between throughput and the rate limits of the API.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be a very slow, serial process and would not be scalable.
Correct: A Pandas UDF is the key to efficient API calls from Spark. It allows you to work with batches of data, which is much more efficient for the API.
Incorrect: A batch size of 1 would be no better than a row-at-a-time UDF. The goal is to use a large batch size to make the API calls more efficient.
Correct: The batch size is a key tuning parameter. You want to make it as large as possible to maximize throughput, but you also need to respect the rate limits of the API you are calling.
questions.explanation: When you are calling an external API from a Spark job, the two most important things for performance and for scalability are to use a Pandas UDF and to tune the batch size. A Pandas UDF allows you to make batch calls to the API, which is much more efficient than making a separate call for each row. The batch size itself is a critical tuning parameter. You need to find the sweet spot that is large enough to get good throughput from the API, but that is not so large that you exceed the API's rate limits. By carefully tuning the batch size, you can build a highly efficient and a highly scalable pipeline for calling any API from Spark.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to evaluate it on a regular basis. They have a limited budget for evaluation. Which of the following is the most cost-effective way to get a regular signal on the quality of the application?
answers: Conducting a large-scale human evaluation with a team of trained annotators every week.
Using an LLM-as-a-judge to evaluate the application on a set of golden test cases on a daily basis.
Relying solely on user feedback.
Manually reviewing a small, random sample of the application's responses each day.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would be very expensive.
Correct: LLM-as-a-judge is a very cost-effective and a very scalable way to get a regular signal on the quality of your application.
Incorrect: While user feedback is valuable and 'free', it is often sparse and biased. It should be used as a supplement to a more systematic evaluation process, not as the only one.

Correct: This can be a surprisingly effective and a very low-cost way to get a regular qualitative signal on the application's performance. It doesn't provide a quantitative metric, but it can be a great way to spot-check the system and to catch any major issues.
questions.explanation: When you are evaluating a RAG application on a limited budget, you need to find cost-effective ways to get a regular signal on its quality. The two best ways to do this are to use an LLM-as-a-judge and to perform regular, manual spot-checks. The LLM-as-a-judge approach provides a scalable and an automated way to get a quantitative measure of the quality. The manual spot-checking provides a low-cost way to get a regular qualitative feel for how the system is performing. The combination of these two techniques can give you a surprisingly good picture of your application's quality without breaking the bank.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that the development team can collaborate effectively. Which TWO of the following Databricks features are most important for enabling collaboration?

Databricks Notebooks, which allow multiple users to edit the same notebook at the same time and to leave comments for each other.
Databricks Repos, which allows the team to use a shared Git repository to manage their code.

Correct: The collaborative features of Databricks Notebooks are a key enabler for team-based development.

Incorrect: While this provides isolation, it does not promote collaboration.
questions.explanation: Effective collaboration is key to the success of any software development project. On Databricks, the two most important features for this are the collaborative notebooks and the integration with Git via Databricks Repos. The collaborative notebooks allow multiple team members to work on the same notebook simultaneously, which is great for pair programming and for code reviews. The integration with Git provides the underlying version control system that is the foundation of all modern, collaborative software development. It allows the team to work on different features in parallel and to merge their changes in a safe and a controlled way.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application and has found that the LLM is sometimes generating answers that are factually correct but are written in a very dry and a very academic tone. The application is for a general audience, and the developer wants the answers to be more engaging and easy to understand. Which of the following is the best way to achieve this?
answers: Fine-tuning the LLM on a large corpus of academic papers.
Using a prompt that includes a persona, for example, 'You are a friendly and enthusiastic science communicator. Explain the following concept in a simple and an engaging way.'
Using a smaller and less capable LLM.
Using a post-processing step to replace any long words with shorter synonyms.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would likely make the tone even more academic.
Correct: Assigning a persona is a very powerful and an easy way to influence the tone and the style of the LLM's response.
Incorrect: A smaller LLM is likely to have less control over its tone.
Incorrect: This would be a very crude and an unreliable way to change the tone of the text. A good prompt is a much better solution.
questions.explanation: Controlling the tone of an LLM is a key skill in prompt engineering. When you want to change the tone from something dry and academic to something more engaging and accessible, the best way to do it is with a well-crafted prompt that includes a persona. By telling the LLM to act as a 'science communicator' or a 'friendly guide', you can significantly shift the style of its output. This is a much more effective and a much more elegant solution than trying to fine-tune the model or to post-process its output.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a large dataset of documents and wants to create embeddings for them. They have a fixed budget and want to get the best possible quality for that budget. Which of the following is the most likely to be the best approach on Databricks?
answers: Using the largest and most expensive proprietary model from a third-party API.
Using a state-of-the-art open-source embedding model and hosting it on a GPU-accelerated Databricks Model Serving endpoint.
Using a very small and a very fast embedding model to save money.
Using a managed foundation model API from Databricks, as these are often priced competitively and are optimized for the platform.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would likely exceed the budget.

Correct: This is often the sweet spot for quality and cost. A good open-source model can provide performance that is very close to the state-of-the-art, and self-hosting it on a GPU endpoint can be very cost-effective at scale.
Incorrect: This would likely result in a significant drop in quality.

Correct: The managed embedding models from Databricks can also be a great option. They are often highly optimized and can provide a very good balance of quality and cost, without the operational overhead of self-hosting.
questions.explanation: When you are trying to get the best possible embedding quality for a fixed budget, you have two great options on Databricks. The first is to use a high-quality, open-source embedding model and to host it yourself on a GPU-accelerated endpoint. This approach gives you a lot of control and can be very cost-effective at scale. The second option is to use one of the managed foundation model APIs from Databricks. These models are often very high-quality and are priced competitively, and they have the added benefit of being a fully managed solution. The best choice between these two will depend on the specific requirements of the project and on the team's expertise.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to monitor its performance. They have a 'golden dataset' of question-answer pairs. Which of the following is a multi-select question asking for TWO of the key metrics that they can calculate using this dataset?
answers: The latency of the application's responses.
The semantic similarity between the generated answer and the golden answer.
The correctness of the generated answer, as determined by a human evaluator or an LLM-as-a-judge who compares it to the golden answer.
The number of users of the application.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Latency is a performance metric and does not require a golden dataset.
Correct: You can use an embedding model to calculate the semantic similarity between the generated answer and the golden answer. This is a good, automated measure of the answer's quality.
Correct: The golden answer provides the ground truth that can be used to evaluate the correctness of the generated answer.
Incorrect: This is a usage metric and does not require a golden dataset.
questions.explanation: A golden dataset is an invaluable asset for evaluating a RAG application. It provides the ground truth that you can use to calculate a wide range of quality metrics. Two of the most common and the most useful metrics that you can calculate with a golden dataset are semantic similarity and correctness. Semantic similarity is an automated metric that can give you a quick, quantitative measure of how close the generated answer is to the ideal answer. Correctness is a more nuanced metric that typically requires a human or an LLM judge to determine if the generated answer is factually correct and contains all the necessary information, using the golden answer as a reference.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to ensure that they can manage the lifecycle of the AI models used in the application, from development to production. Which TWO of the following Databricks features are most essential for this?
answers: Databricks SQL.
The MLflow Model Registry.
Unity Catalog.
Databricks Repos.

Correct: The Model Registry is the central hub for managing the lifecycle of ML models on Databricks. It allows you to version, to stage, and to govern your models as they move from development to production.

Correct: Unity Catalog is the unified governance layer for all data and AI assets, including models. By registering your models in Unity Catalog, you can manage them with the same governance policies as your data.
Incorrect: While Repos are important for managing the code, the Model Registry and Unity Catalog are the key tools for managing the models themselves.
questions.explanation: Managing the lifecycle of AI models is a key part of MLOps. On Databricks, the two most essential features for this are the MLflow Model Registry and Unity Catalog. The Model Registry provides the core functionality for versioning and for staging your models. Unity Catalog provides the overarching governance layer, allowing you to manage your models as first-class citizens in your data estate. By using these two features together, you can create a robust and a well-governed process for managing the entire lifecycle of your RAG application's models.

questions.question: A developer is building a RAG application that needs to answer questions that are outside of its knowledge base. For example, 'What is the weather like in London right now?' Which of the following is the best way to handle this?
answers: Fine-tuning the LLM on a large dataset of weather information.
Creating a LangChain agent that has a tool for calling a real-time weather API.
Telling the user that the application cannot answer questions about the weather.
Trying to answer the question based on the LLM's pre-trained knowledge.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not provide real-time information.
Correct: This is the perfect use case for an agent with a tool. The agent can recognize that the question is about weather and can use the weather tool to get the real-time information.

Correct: This is another valid, and often simpler, approach. If the primary goal of the application is to answer questions about a specific knowledge base, it can be a good design choice to have it gracefully decline to answer out-of-scope questions.
Incorrect: The LLM's pre-trained knowledge is not up-to-date and would not be able to provide the current weather.
questions.explanation: When a RAG application receives a question that is outside of its knowledge base, you have two main design choices. The first is to extend the application's capabilities by giving it access to an external tool, such as a weather API. This can be done very effectively with a LangChain agent. The second choice is to have the application recognize that the question is out-of-scope and to gracefully inform the user that it cannot answer. The best choice will depend on the specific goals of the application. For a general-purpose assistant, the agent-based approach is better. For a more focused, domain-specific application, the second approach is often simpler and safer.

questions.question: A data engineer is working with a dataset of documents that have a clear hierarchical structure (e.g., chapters, sections, sub-sections). Which of the following is the most effective chunking strategy?
answers: Fixed-size chunking.
Recursive character text splitting, with the separators defined based on the hierarchical structure of the documents.
Semantic chunking.
Creating a separate chunk for each word in the document.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This would not respect the hierarchical structure of the documents.

Correct: A recursive character text splitter is the perfect tool for this. You can configure it to split by the highest level of the hierarchy first (e.g., chapters), and then to recursively split the resulting chunks by the lower levels of the hierarchy.
Incorrect: While a good technique, for a document with a very clear and an explicit hierarchical structure, a structure-aware approach like recursive splitting is often more direct and more reliable.
Incorrect: This would create chunks that are far too small and that have no semantic meaning.
questions.explanation:
When your documents have a clear, hierarchical structure, the best chunking strategy is one that can leverage that structure. A recursive character text splitter is the ideal tool for this. You can provide it with a list of separators that corresponds to the hierarchy of your documents (e.g., `['

Chapter ', '

Section ', '

']`). The splitter will then intelligently break down the documents along these structural boundaries, which will result in a set of very high-quality, semantically coherent chunks.

questions.question: A company has deployed a RAG application and wants to monitor it for fairness and to ensure that it is not providing biased answers to different groups of users. Which of the following is the most effective way to do this?
answers: Assuming that since they are using a well-known foundation model, it will not have any biases.
On a regular basis, running the application on a specialized 'bias benchmark' dataset and analyzing the results to see if there are any performance differences across different demographic groups.
Conducting 'red teaming' exercises where testers with diverse backgrounds try to elicit biased responses from the model.
Asking the LLM if it is biased.
feedbacks: Incorrect: All large language models have biases that are learned from the data they were trained on.
Correct: This is a systematic and a quantitative way to test for and to monitor for bias.
Correct: Red teaming is a powerful qualitative technique for finding unexpected and subtle biases in a model.
Incorrect: An LLM is not a reliable source of information about its own biases.
questions.explanation: Ensuring the fairness of a RAG application is a critical part of a responsible AI practice. The two most effective ways to monitor for bias are to use a quantitative bias benchmark and to conduct qualitative red teaming exercises. A bias benchmark is a specialized dataset that is designed to test for known types of social and demographic biases. By running this benchmark on a regular basis, you can get a quantitative measure of your model's fairness. Red teaming is a more open-ended, adversarial process where you actively try to find the biases in your model. The combination of these two techniques provides a robust and a comprehensive approach to fairness monitoring.

questions.question: A company is building a RAG application and wants to follow MLOps best practices for managing the application's lifecycle. Which TWO of the following are the most important components of an MLOps for RAG workflow on Databricks?
answers: A process for manually deploying the application by copying the files to a server.
A CI/CD pipeline to automate the testing and the deployment of the application.
A centralized model registry (like the MLflow Model Registry, integrated with Unity Catalog) to version and to govern the RAG chain and other AI assets.
A single developer who is responsible for all aspects of the application.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the opposite of an MLOps best practice.
Correct: A CI/CD pipeline is the engine of a modern MLOps workflow.
Correct: A central, governed model registry is a cornerstone of MLOps. It provides the single source of truth for all your AI models.
Incorrect: MLOps is a team sport that requires collaboration between development, operations, and data science.
